title: Essential Hypertension: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACC/AHA & JAMA)
snippet: Meta-analysis confirms lowering SBP by 10 mmHg reduces major cardiovascular events by 20%, stroke by 27%, and heart failure by 28%. First-line pharmacological classes (thiazide diuretics, CCBs, ACEi/ARBs) demonstrate equivalent mortality reduction; CCBs excel in stroke prevention (RR 0.82), while ACEi/ARBs offer superior renal protection in diabetic cohorts (HR 0.68). Guideline Protocol: DASH diet adherence (approx. 11 mmHg SBP reduction in hypertensive adults); dietary sodium restriction to <1,500 mg/day (or at least 1,000 mg/day reduction); aerobic exercise 90-150 min/week; potassium supplementation (3,500-5,000 mg/day via diet unless CKD present). Thresholds: Stage 1: 130-139 / 80-89 mmHg (lifestyle modification + 10-year ASCVD risk stratification); Stage 2: ≥140/90 mmHg (lifestyle + combination guideline therapy).

patient_plain_language: Blood pressure is the force of blood pushing against the walls of your arteries. When it stays high, it slowly damages your blood vessels like running water at too high a pressure through household pipes.

solution_protocol.non_pharmacological_targets: DASH diet adherence (approx. 11 mmHg SBP reduction in hypertensive adults); dietary sodium restriction to <1,500 mg/day (or at least 1,000 mg/day reduction); aerobic exercise 90-150 min/week; potassium supplementation (3,500-5,000 mg/day via diet unless CKD present).
solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Standardized home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM): 2 morning and 2 evening readings for 7 consecutive days prior to clinical review.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Stage 1: 130-139 / 80-89 mmHg (lifestyle modification + 10-year ASCVD risk stratification); Stage 2: ≥140/90 mmHg (lifestyle + combination guideline therapy).

disease: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF)
title: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (PARADIGM-HF))
keywords: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (hfref)
snippet: In 8,442 patients with HFrEF (LVEF ≤40%), Sacubitril/Valsartan reduced composite CV death or heart failure hospitalization by 20% compared to Enalapril (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.73-0.87; p<0.001). All-cause mortality was reduced by 16% (p<0.001). Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) establishes foundational four-pillar therapy: ARNI/ACEi, beta-blockers, MRA, and SGLT2i. Guideline Protocol: Daily morning weight tracking; sodium restriction to <2,000-3,000 mg/day; fluid moderation (1.5-2.0 L/day) in congested patients; structured cardiac rehabilitation program. Thresholds: Monitor LVEF via echocardiogram every 6-12 months following optimization of medical therapy.

solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Monitor LVEF via echocardiogram every 6-12 months following optimization of medical therapy.

title: Atrial Fibrillation & Stroke Prophylaxis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (ARISTOTLE))
snippet: Apixaban was superior to Warfarin in preventing stroke or systemic embolism (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.66-0.95; p=0.01 for superiority) with a 31% reduction in major bleeding (HR 0.69; 95% CI 0.60-0.80; p<0.001) and a significant reduction in all-cause mortality (HR 0.89; p=0.047). ACC/AHA guidelines strongly recommend DOACs over vitamin K antagonists in non-valvular AF. Guideline Protocol: Strict alcohol cessation/reduction; screening and management of obstructive sleep apnea; weight loss target of ≥10% in obese patients to reduce AF recurrence. Thresholds: Anticoagulation recommended based on CHA2DS2-VASc score (≥2 in males, ≥3 in females).

patient_plain_language: Atrial fibrillation is an irregular, quivering heartbeat in the top chambers of your heart. Because blood does not pump out smoothly, it can pool and form clots that travel to the brain, causing a stroke.

doctor_consultation_checklist.parameter_question: What is my CHA2DS2-VASc stroke risk score, and what does it mean for my treatment plan?

red_flags: Sudden facial droop, arm weakness, or speech slurring (FAST criteria for stroke)
Uncontrolled bleeding from minor cuts, coughing up blood, or black tarry stools

solution_protocol.non_pharmacological_targets: Strict alcohol cessation/reduction; screening and management of obstructive sleep apnea; weight loss target of ≥10% in obese patients to reduce AF recurrence.
solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Annual renal function (CrCl/eGFR) assessment to ensure appropriate DOAC dosing cutoffs (more frequent if CrCl 30-50 mL/min).
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Anticoagulation recommended based on CHA2DS2-VASc score (≥2 in males, ≥3 in females).

title: Hypercholesterolemia & Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (ASCVD): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AHA/ACC/Multisociety)
snippet: Extensive meta-analyses of Cholesterol Treatment Trialists (CTT) show a 21% reduction in major vascular events per 1.0 mmol/L (~39 mg/dL) reduction in LDL-C. High-intensity statin therapy reduces LDL-C by ≥50%, moderate-intensity by 30-49%. Addition of non-statins (Ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors) yields proportional additional cardiovascular event risk reductions. Guideline Protocol: Mediterranean or plant-forward dietary pattern: saturated fat <7% of total calories; elimination of trans fats; 25-30 g/day dietary fiber (7-13 g soluble fiber). Thresholds: Primary prevention: 10-year ASCVD risk threshold ≥7.5% warrants statin discussion; secondary prevention: target LDL-C <55 mg/dL (<1.4 mmol/L) in very high-risk individuals.

Sudden shortness of breath on mild exertion

solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Primary prevention: 10-year ASCVD risk threshold ≥7.5% warrants statin discussion; secondary prevention: target LDL-C <55 mg/dL (<1.4 mmol/L) in very high-risk individuals.

title: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) & Pulmonary Embolism (PE): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (CHEST)
snippet: CHEST guidelines strongly recommend DOACs (Apixaban, Rivaroxaban, Dabigatran, Edoxaban) over Vitamin K antagonists for initial and long-term VTE management in non-cancer patients (Grade 1B). Minimum treatment duration for provoked VTE is 3 months; extended unprovoked VTE anticoagulation carries a >80% relative risk reduction in recurrent thrombosis. Guideline Protocol: Early ambulation over bed rest once therapeutic anticoagulation is started; graduated compression stockings for symptom relief in post-thrombotic syndrome. Thresholds: Diagnostic workup driven by validated clinical prediction scores (Wells DVT/PE score) followed by high-sensitivity D-dimer or compression ultrasonography/CT pulmonary angiography.

title: Stable Ischemic Heart Disease & Angina: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (ISCHEMIA))
snippet: In 5,179 patients with moderate or severe ischemia, an initial invasive strategy (angiography and revascularization plus medical therapy) did not reduce major ischemic cardiovascular events or all-cause death compared to an initial conservative strategy of optimal medical therapy alone (cumulative 5-year event rate 13.3% vs. 15.5%; p=0.34). Revascularization improved quality of life and angina symptoms in daily angina sufferers. Guideline Protocol: Supervised exercise training (30-60 min of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise 5+ days/week); smoking cessation (absolute risk reduction of CV events >30%); stress management protocols. Thresholds: Revascularization reserved for failure of optimal medical therapy to control symptoms or left main stem/high-risk anatomy.

title: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ADA)
snippet: Targeted HbA1c control (<7.0% for most non-pregnant adults) significantly reduces microvascular complications (retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy). For individuals with established ASCVD, heart failure, or CKD, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists confer organ-protective benefits independent of baseline HbA1c or background metformin use (UKPDS, EMPA-REG, LEADER). Guideline Protocol: Weight reduction goal of ≥5-10% to improve glycemic control; 150 min/week moderate-to-vigorous aerobic exercise plus 2-3 sessions resistance training; carbohydrate counting and reduction in ultra-processed sugars. Thresholds: Standard glycemic target: HbA1c <7.0% (53 mmol/mol); pre-prandial glucose 80-130 mg/dL; post-prandial glucose <180 mg/dL.

patient_plain_language: In type 2 diabetes, your body’s cells become resistant to insulin—the key that lets sugar enter your cells for energy. Because the lock doesn't work, sugar builds up in your bloodstream.

Blood glucose <70 mg/dL with confusion, sweating, shakiness, or loss of consciousness

solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Standard glycemic target: HbA1c <7.0% (53 mmol/mol); pre-prandial glucose 80-130 mg/dL; post-prandial glucose <180 mg/dL.

title: Obesity & Weight Management: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (SURMOUNT-1))
snippet: In 2,539 adults with obesity, Tirzepatide (dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist) at 15 mg weekly achieved a mean weight reduction of 20.9% (-23.6 kg) at 72 weeks compared to 3.1% in placebo (p<0.001). Over 91% of participants in the 15 mg cohort achieved ≥5% weight loss, accompanied by significant reductions in blood pressure, fasting insulin, and lipid parameters. Guideline Protocol: Prescribed energy deficit of 500-750 kcal/day; high dietary protein intake (1.2-1.5 g/kg ideal body weight) combined with resistance training to preserve lean skeletal muscle mass during weight loss. Thresholds: Pharmacotherapy indicated for BMI ≥30 kg/m², or BMI ≥27 kg/m² with at least one weight-related comorbidity (e.g., hypertension, dyslipidemia, T2D, OSA).

title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH / NASH): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (MAESTRO-NASH))
snippet: In 966 patients with biopsy-proven MASH and fibrosis stages F1B-F3, Resmetirom (thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist) achieved MASH resolution with no worsening of fibrosis in 29.9% (100 mg) vs. 9.7% (placebo) (p<0.001), and fibrosis improvement of at least one stage with no worsening of NAFLD activity score in 25.9% vs. 14.2% (p<0.001). Guideline Protocol: 7-10% total body weight reduction leads to steatohepatitis resolution and possible fibrosis regression; complete elimination of sugar-sweetened beverages and high-fructose corn syrup; Mediterranean dietary pattern. Thresholds: FIB-4 score <1.30 rules out advanced fibrosis with high negative predictive value (>90%); FIB-4 >2.67 indicates high risk requiring hepatology evaluation.

patient_plain_language: MASH is an advanced form of fatty liver where excess fat stored in liver cells causes inflammation and scarring (fibrosis), similar to how skin forms a scar after an injury.

solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: FIB-4 score <1.30 rules out advanced fibrosis with high negative predictive value (>90%); FIB-4 >2.67 indicates high risk requiring hepatology evaluation.

title: Primary Hypothyroidism: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ATA / AACE)
snippet: Guidelines establish Levothyroxine monotherapy as standard of care. Full replacement dose is approximately 1.6 mcg/kg/day in healthy adults, with lower initiation doses (25-50 mcg) in elderly patients or those with coronary artery disease to avoid precipitating cardiac ischemia. Routine addition of Liothyronine (T3) is not recommended by consensus due to lack of sustained RCT benefit. Guideline Protocol: Strict administration timing: Take on an empty stomach with a full glass of water 30-60 minutes before breakfast, or at bedtime (3-4 hours after the last meal); separate by ≥4 hours from calcium, iron, or antacids. Thresholds: Target TSH range: 0.5-4.5 mIU/L (adjusted to 4.0-7.0 mIU/L in elderly adults >70-80 years to prevent overreplacement osteopenia/AFib).

title: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ESHRE / ASRM / Monash)
snippet: Diagnosis confirmed via Rotterdam criteria (2 of 3: oligo/anovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound). Lifestyle intervention is first-line management for all presentations. Combined oral contraceptives are first-line pharmacological treatment for irregular cycles and hirsutism. Metformin is recommended for metabolic features and glycemic control (SMD -0.45 on BMI/insulin). Letrozole is first-line ovulation induction agent over Clomiphene (NEJM PPCOS II). Guideline Protocol: 5-10% weight loss restores regular ovulatory cycles in up to 50% of women; regular physical activity (minimum 150 min/week moderate intensity plus muscle strengthening); low glycemic index dietary emphasis. Thresholds: Endometrial protection protocol: ensure at least 4 withdrawal bleeds per year to prevent endometrial hyperplasia.

title: Adult Persistent Asthma: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (GINA)
snippet: GINA Track 1 establishes low-dose ICS-Formoterol as the preferred reliever across all asthma severities. SYGMA 1 and 2 trials (NEJM 2018) proved as-needed ICS-Formoterol reduces severe exacerbations by 60-64% compared to SABA-only therapy, while reducing steroid exposure by 75-83%. SABA monotherapy is strongly discouraged due to increased risk of airway hyperresponsiveness and death. Guideline Protocol: Identification and mitigation of environmental triggers (tobacco smoke, indoor dust mites, animal dander, mold); written personalized Asthma Action Plan; inhaler technique demonstration at every clinical visit. Thresholds: Step-up or step-down evaluation based on symptom control validated questionnaires (e.g., Asthma Control Test [ACT] score ≥20 indicates control).

title: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (GOLD & NEJM (ETHOS))
snippet: ETHOS trial (n=8,509) demonstrated single-inhaler triple therapy (ICS/LAMA/LABA) significantly reduced the rate of moderate or severe COPD exacerbations by 24% compared to LAMA/LABA dual therapy (p<0.001) and reduced all-cause mortality by 46% in patients with blood eosinophil counts ≥100 cells/μL and history of exacerbations. Guideline Protocol: Smoking cessation is the only intervention proven to slow FEV1 decline; pulmonary rehabilitation program (demonstrates Grade A evidence for reducing dyspnea and hospital admissions); pneumococcal, influenza, COVID-19, and RSV vaccinations. Thresholds: Blood eosinophil count <100 cells/μL identifies patients unlikely to benefit from inhaled corticosteroids (increased pneumonia risk).

title: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ATS / IDSA)
snippet: Clinical guideline establishes CURB-65 or Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) to determine outpatient vs. inpatient site of care. For healthy outpatients without comorbidities, monotherapy with Amoxicillin (1 g TID) or Doxycycline is strongly recommended over macrolides due to widespread pneumococcal resistance. For patients with comorbidities, combination therapy (beta-lactam + macrolide) or respiratory fluoroquinolones is recommended. Guideline Protocol: Adequate oral hydration; early mobilization; temporary smoking cessation; fever management. title: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (DAPA-CKD) & KDIGO)
snippet: DAPA-CKD trial (n=4,304) demonstrated that in patients with eGFR 25-75 mL/min/1.73m² and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR) 200-5000 mg/g, Dapagliflozin reduced the composite risk of sustained ≥50% eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, or renal/CV death by 39% (HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.51-0.72; p<0.001). snippet: Primary diagnosis requires serologic IgA tissue transglutaminase (tTG-IgA) testing with concurrent total IgA levels to rule out IgA deficiency. Guideline Protocol: Strict elimination of all dietary gluten sources (wheat, rye, barley); consultation with an expert celiac clinical dietitian; education on preventing food cross-contamination in home kitchens. Thresholds: Patients must maintain an active, gluten-containing diet prior to diagnostic testing to avoid false-negative serologies and biopsies.

If disease activity remains moderate or high despite optimized oral/subcutaneous MTX, adding a biologic DMARD (TNF inhibitor) or targeted synthetic DMARD is recommended. Guideline Protocol: Joint-protective low-impact aerobic exercise and resistance training; hand therapy / occupational splinting; anti-inflammatory dietary emphasis; complete smoking cessation (smoking reduces MTX efficacy and worsens joint erosion). Thresholds: Target: CDAI score ≤2.8 (remission) or ≤10 (low disease activity).

title: Knee & Hip Osteoarthritis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (OARSI & ACR)
snippet: Core treatments strongly recommended for all individuals: structured land-based exercise, dietary weight management, and disease education. Topical NSAIDs (Diclofenac gel) are strongly recommended as first-line pharmacotherapy for knee OA due to equivalent analgesia to oral NSAIDs with minimal systemic adverse events. Oral opioids are strongly recommended against due to lack of long-term benefit and high toxicity. Guideline Protocol: Weight loss target of ≥5-10% in overweight patients (significantly reduces compressive knee joint loading forces by 4-fold); low-impact quadriceps strengthening, cycling, or aquatic exercise; assistive walking canes in contralateral hand. Thresholds: Total joint arthroplasty referral reserved for advanced structural joint damage with intractable pain and loss of independent mobility despite conservative therapy.

title: Gout & Hyperuricemia: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACR)
snippet: Strong recommendation for a Treat-to-Target urate-lowering strategy. Allopurinol is the preferred first-line xanthine oxidase inhibitor. Indications for urate-lowering therapy (ULT): ≥1 subcutaneous tophi, radiographic damage, or ≥2 flares/year. Starting ULT at low dose (Allopurinol ≤100 mg/day, lower in CKD) and titrating upward to achieve target serum urate prevents mobilization flares. Guideline Protocol: Limiting intake of purine-rich foods (organ meats, shellfish), high-fructose corn syrup, and alcohol (especially beer); maintaining adequate daily water hydration; weight loss in overweight individuals. Thresholds: Serum urate target: <6.0 mg/dL (<360 μmol/L) for all patients (<5.0 mg/dL if tophi present) to ensure crystal dissolution.

title: Chronic Non-Specific Lower Back Pain: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACP & The Lancet Series)
snippet: ACP guidelines recommend that clinicians and patients initially select nonpharmacological treatment with exercise, multidisciplinary rehabilitation, acupuncture, mindfulness-based stress reduction, or spinal manipulation (Grade: strong recommendation). Pharmacological therapy is secondary (NSAIDs first-line, Duloxetine second-line). Routine MRI imaging is strongly discouraged without red flags as it increases surgery rates without improving clinical outcomes. Guideline Protocol: Active physical therapy focusing on core stabilization, directional preference exercises, and graded active movement; avoidance of prolonged bed rest; cognitive behavioral approaches to address fear-avoidance behaviors. Thresholds: Imaging only indicated if pain persists >6 weeks with no response to therapy or if progressive neurological deficits appear.

patient_plain_language: Most lower back pain is related to muscle strain, ligament tension, and spinal disc irritation. Resting in bed actually delays recovery; gentle, steady movement is the best medicine for healing.

title: Postmenopausal Osteoporosis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Endocrine Society)
snippet: Guidelines recommend initial treatment with oral bisphosphonates (Alendronate, Risedronate) or IV Zoledronic acid for postmenopausal women at high risk of fractures, reducing vertebral fractures by ~50-70% and hip fractures by ~40% (FIT and HORIZON trials). In women at very high risk (T-score <-3.0 or prior fracture), an anabolic regimen (Teriparatide, Romosozumab) followed by antiresorptive therapy is recommended. Guideline Protocol: Daily total calcium intake of 1,200 mg (via diet preferred); Vitamin D3 supplementation to maintain serum 25(OH)D levels >30 ng/mL; weight-bearing and resistance exercises; home fall-prevention evaluation (removing tripping hazards, grab bars). Thresholds: Osteoporosis defined by DEXA T-score ≤-2.5 at femoral neck or lumbar spine, or FRAX 10-year major osteoporotic fracture risk ≥20% / hip fracture risk ≥3%.

title: Menopausal Vasomotor Symptoms & Hormone Therapy: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (The Menopause Society (NAMS) & JAMA)
snippet: Systemic hormone therapy is the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms and the genitourinary syndrome of menopause. In women aged <60 years or within 10 years of menopause onset, the benefit-risk ratio is favorable for relief of hot flashes and fracture prevention without increased all-cause mortality. Women with an intact uterus require concurrent progestogen (e.g., micronized progesterone) to prevent endometrial cancer. Guideline Protocol: Layered breathable clothing; keeping ambient bedroom temperatures cool; avoidance of hot beverages, alcohol, and spicy foods; clinical hypnosis or cognitive behavioral therapy for hot flashes (Level 1 evidence for symptom reduction). Thresholds: Transdermal estradiol preferred over oral route in women with elevated baseline VTE risk, hypertension, or hypertriglyceridemia.

title: Endometriosis & Chronic Pelvic Pain: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ESHRE)
snippet: ESHRE guidelines recommend empirical medical treatment without requiring laparoscopic confirmation in patients with clinical suspicion. Combined oral contraceptives or progestogens (Dienogest 2 mg) are first-line hormonal therapies (Grade A). GnRH receptor antagonists (Elagolix, Relugolix; ELARIS trials, NEJM) significantly reduce dysmenorrhea and non-menstrual pelvic pain with add-back therapy to preserve bone density. Guideline Protocol: Pelvic floor physical therapy to address secondary pelvic myofascial pain and hypertonicity; transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS); anti-inflammatory dietary approaches. Thresholds: Laparoscopic surgical excision indicated when medical treatment fails, when ovarian endometriomas >3 cm are present, or in deep infiltrating bowel/bladder disease.

title: Preeclampsia Prevention & Management: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (USPSTF & ACOG)
snippet: The USPSTF and ACOG recommend low-dose aspirin (81-150 mg/day) prophylaxis initiated between 12 and 16 weeks of gestation (and continued until delivery) in pregnant individuals at high risk for preeclampsia (Grade B). Meta-analyses (ASPRE trial, NEJM) confirm low-dose aspirin reduces preterm preeclampsia by ~62% and intrauterine growth restriction by ~20%. Guideline Protocol: Frequent prenatal blood pressure monitoring; standardized protein-to-creatinine ratio (uPCR) testing; patient education on early symptom recognition. Thresholds: Preeclampsia defined as BP ≥140/90 mmHg after 20 weeks gestation accompanied by proteinuria (uPCR ≥0.3 mg/mg) or new signs of end-organ dysfunction (thrombocytopenia, renal insufficiency, elevated transaminases).

title: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACOG & HAPO Study)
snippet: HAPO study demonstrated strong, continuous linear associations between maternal glucose levels and adverse outcomes (birth weight >90th percentile, primary cesarean delivery, and neonatal hypoglycemia). First-line management is medical nutrition therapy and moderate exercise, which successfully manages 70-85% of GDM pregnancies. Insulin is the preferred first-line pharmacological treatment when glycemic goals are not met. Guideline Protocol: Individualized medical nutrition therapy emphasizing complex carbohydrates distributed across 3 meals and 2-3 snacks; post-prandial walking (15-30 minutes after meals improves glucose levels). Thresholds: ACOG Glycemic targets: Fasting blood glucose <95 mg/dL; 1-hour postprandial <140 mg/dL; or 2-hour postprandial <120 mg/dL.

title: Pediatric Acute Otitis Media (AOM): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAP)
snippet: AAP guidelines emphasize watchful waiting with initial pain management for 48-72 hours in children ≥2 years with uncomplicated unilateral AOM and mild symptoms, reducing unnecessary antibiotic exposure. When antibiotics are indicated (severe pain, fever ≥39°C, bilateral in children <2 years), high-dose Amoxicillin (80-90 mg/kg/day divided BID) is first-line to eradicate resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae. Guideline Protocol: Immediate, aggressive pain control using weight-based oral acetaminophen or ibuprofen; avoidance of secondhand tobacco smoke exposure; encouragement of breastfeeding; avoidance of bottle propping in bed. Thresholds: Diagnostic criteria require moderate-to-severe bulging of the tympanic membrane or new onset otorrhea not due to acute otitis externa.

title: Pediatric Asthma & Viral Wheeze: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (GINA)
snippet: For children ≤5 years with recurrent viral wheezing and intermittent symptoms, short-acting beta-2 agonists (SABA) via pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI) with a valved holding chamber and mask are recommended. Daily controller therapy with low-dose inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) is indicated if symptom pattern is frequent (>3 episodes/year) or severe, significantly reducing exacerbation days and hospital admissions (CAMP study, NEJM). Guideline Protocol: Mandatory use of a spacer chamber with an appropriately sized face mask for all young children; elimination of indoor environmental tobacco smoke and wood smoke; avoidance of known pet or dust triggers. Thresholds: Step-down controller therapy should be considered once stability is maintained for 3 consecutive months.

title: Simple Febrile Seizures: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAP)
snippet: Simple febrile seizures (generalized, lasting <15 minutes, occurring once in 24 hours in a child aged 6-60 months) carry no increased risk of long-term neurological damage, intellectual disability, or significant epilepsy risk compared to the general population. Routine EEG, brain CT/MRI, and routine lumbar puncture are not recommended in well-appearing, fully immunized children with simple febrile seizures. Guideline Protocol: Immediate parent education: During a seizure, gently place child on their side (recovery position) on a soft surface, do not restrain them, never place anything in their mouth, time the duration; antipyretics provide comfort but do not prevent seizure recurrence. Thresholds: Complex febrile seizure defined if focal features exist, duration >15 minutes, or recurs within 24 hours (requires thorough neurological evaluation).

title: Pediatric Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAP & MTA Study)
snippet: For preschool children (ages 4-5), parent training in behavior management (PTBM) is first-line treatment (Grade A). Guideline Protocol: Behavioral parent training; classroom accommodations (504 Plan or Individualized Education Program [IEP]); structured daily routines, visual checklists, and positive reinforcement systems. title: COVID-19 Acute Outpatient Management: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (EPIC-HR) & WHO)
snippet: In nonhospitalized high-risk adult outpatients, oral Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir (Paxlovid) initiated within 5 days of symptom onset reduced COVID-19-related hospitalization or death by 89% compared to placebo (0.77% vs 6.31%; p<0.001). IV Remdesivir for 3 days represents an alternative high-efficacy antiviral option (PINETREE trial, 87% reduction). Concomitant drug interaction check is mandatory due to strong CYP3A4 inhibition by ritonavir. Guideline Protocol: Strict isolation according to public health guidelines; oral hydration; fever and body ache management with acetaminophen; prone resting positions. Thresholds: Treatment must be initiated within 5 days of symptom onset. Dose adjustment mandatory in moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-59 mL/min: 150 mg nirmatrelvir / 100 mg ritonavir BID); contraindicated in eGFR <30 mL/min.

title: Atopic Dermatitis (Eczema): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAD)
snippet: AAD guidelines emphasize basic barrier repair with bland emollient ointments as foundational therapy. Topical corticosteroids (TCS) are first-line prescription therapy for flares. Topical calcineurin inhibitors (Tacrolimus) and PDE-4 inhibitors (Crisaborole) are recommended for sensitive areas (face, neck, skin folds). For moderate-to-severe disease refractory to topicals, biologic therapy with Dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα; LIBERTY AD trials, NEJM) provides significant clearance with an excellent safety profile. Guideline Protocol: 'Soak and Seal' routine: Daily lukewarm baths/showers (5-10 minutes) followed immediately within 3 minutes by liberal application of thick petrolatum- or ceramide-based ointments; use of gentle, fragrance-free cleansers; wearing loose 100% cotton clothing. Thresholds: Assess disease severity using validated tools like EASI (Eczema Area and Severity Index) or SCORAD.

patient_plain_language: Eczema is a condition where your skin's outer moisture barrier is leaky and easily inflamed, allowing water to escape and irritants to enter, causing intensely itchy, red, cracked patches.

Spreading honey-colored crusted sores or skin that feels hot, swollen, and tender (Bacterial superinfection)

solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Reassess flare frequency at 4-8 weeks; transition to proactive twice-weekly maintenance application of topical therapies to previous flare sites.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Assess disease severity using validated tools like EASI (Eczema Area and Severity Index) or SCORAD.

title: Plaque Psoriasis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAD / NPF)
snippet: For localized disease (<3% body surface area), high-potency topical corticosteroids combined with vitamin D analogues (Calcipotriene) are first-line. For moderate-to-severe disease (≥3-5% BSA or sensitive areas), targeted biologics (anti-IL-23: Risankizumab, Guselkumab; anti-IL-17: Secukinumab, Ixekizumab; anti-TNF: Adalimumab) achieve PASI 90 or PASI 100 skin clearance rates in 70-85% of patients (Phase 3 trials, NEJM/Lancet). Guideline Protocol: Regular daily emollient moisturization; screening for metabolic comorbidities (obesity, hypertension, diabetes) and cardiovascular risk reduction; smoking cessation; screening for psoriatic arthritis. Thresholds: Target: BSA <1% or PASI 90 response at 12-16 weeks.

Sudden widespread eruption of small sterile pustules covering the body with fever (Generalized Pustular Psoriasis)

solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Target: BSA <1% or PASI 90 response at 12-16 weeks.

title: Cellulitis & Purulent Skin Infections: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (IDSA)
snippet: IDSA guidelines classify SSTIs into purulent (abscess, furuncle) and non-purulent (cellulitis, erysipelas). For non-purulent cellulitis, beta-lactam monotherapy covering Streptococcus (Cephalexin or Cefazolin) is recommended (5-day course proven equivalent to 10 days in JAMA RCT). For purulent infections, incision and drainage is the primary therapy; empirical CA-MRSA antibiotic coverage (Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or Doxycycline) is added for systemic signs. Guideline Protocol: Elevation of the affected limb above the level of the heart to promote lymphatic drainage and accelerate resolution; skin demarcation with a pen line to monitor boundary progression; treatment of predisposing factors (e.g., tinea pedis athlete's foot). Thresholds: Hospital admission indicated for systemic toxicity, hemodynamic instability, or failure of oral therapy after 48-72 hours.

solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Reassess at 48 hours. Mild expansion of erythema in the first 24-48 hours can occur due to bacterial toxin release despite effective killing.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Hospital admission indicated for systemic toxicity, hemodynamic instability, or failure of oral therapy after 48-72 hours.

title: Clostridioides difficile Infection (CDI): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (IDSA / SHEA)
snippet: Guidelines strongly recommend Fidaxomicin (200 mg BID for 10 days) over oral Vancomycin (125 mg QID for 10 days) as the preferred initial treatment for non-severe and severe CDI (Grade: conditional recommendation), demonstrating superior sustained clinical response and significantly lower recurrence rates. Metronidazole is strongly discouraged. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) is recommended for multiple recurrent CDI. Guideline Protocol: Immediate discontinuation of the inciting antibiotic if clinically feasible; strict contact precautions and hand hygiene with soap and water (alcohol sanitizers do not kill C. diff spores); avoid antimotility agents (e.g., Loperamide). Thresholds: Severe CDI defined by WBC ≥15,000 cells/μL or serum creatinine >1.5 mg/dL.

solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Severe CDI defined by WBC ≥15,000 cells/μL or serum creatinine >1.5 mg/dL.

title: Early Localized Lyme Disease: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (IDSA / AAN / ACR)
snippet: Patients with characteristic erythema migrans (EM) rash and history of potential tick exposure in an endemic area should be diagnosed and treated clinically without serologic testing (serology is insensitive in early localized disease, <40%). Oral Doxycycline (100 mg BID for 10-14 days) is first-line treatment. Single-dose prophylactic Doxycycline (200 mg) is recommended within 72 hours of removing an attached Ixodes scapularis tick after ≥36 hours of attachment. Guideline Protocol: Tick prevention education: Insect repellents with DEET or picaridin; wearing permethrin-treated clothing; full-body tick checks within 2 hours of outdoor exposure in wooded/grassy areas; tick removal using fine-tipped tweezers pulling straight up. Thresholds: Two-tiered serological testing (ELISA followed by Western Blot or second enzyme immunoassay) reserved for disseminated disease stages (carditis, facial palsy, arthritis).

solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Two-tiered serological testing (ELISA followed by Western Blot or second enzyme immunoassay) reserved for disseminated disease stages (carditis, facial palsy, arthritis).

title: Colorectal Cancer Screening: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (USPSTF)
snippet: The USPSTF recommends screening for colorectal cancer in all adults aged 45 to 75 years (Grade A). Multiple screening strategies demonstrate strong mortality reduction: Colonoscopy every 10 years, annual Fecal Immunochemical Test (FIT), or stool DNA-FIT (Cologuard) every 3 years. Any positive non-invasive stool test mandates follow-up diagnostic colonoscopy. Guideline Protocol: High dietary fiber intake; regular aerobic exercise; limitation of red and processed meats; smoking cessation and reduction in alcohol intake. Thresholds: Screening begins earlier (age 40 or 10 years before the youngest affected first-degree relative's diagnosis) in individuals with a family history of colorectal cancer.

title: Breast Cancer Screening: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (USPSTF)
snippet: The USPSTF recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years (Grade B). Collaborative modeling indicates that starting screening at age 40 rather than age 50 averts an additional 1.3 breast cancer deaths per 1,000 women screened, with favorable benefit-to-harm ratios regarding false-positive mammograms and benign biopsies. Guideline Protocol: Regular aerobic exercise; weight management post-menopause; limitation of alcohol intake (alcohol is a dose-dependent breast cancer risk factor); breast self-awareness of any changes. Thresholds: Formal hereditary risk assessment (e.g., Tyrer-Cuzick model) and genetic counseling for BRCA1/2 recommended if significant family history of breast/ovarian cancer is present.

title: Lung Cancer Screening: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (USPSTF & NEJM (NLST))
snippet: The USPSTF recommends annual screening for lung cancer with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) in adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years (Grade B). The National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) demonstrated a 20% relative reduction in lung cancer mortality with LDCT compared to chest radiography. Guideline Protocol: Immediate, evidence-based smoking cessation counseling and pharmacotherapy at every screening encounter (smoking cessation reduces lung cancer mortality by >50% over time); radon exposure testing in the home. Thresholds: Lung-RADS structured reporting criteria used to classify pulmonary nodule findings and dictate follow-up intervals.

title: Cervical Cancer Screening & HPV Triage: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (USPSTF & ASCCP)
snippet: USPSTF recommends screening for cervical cancer in women aged 21 to 65 years. Strategies: Cervical cytology (Pap smear) alone every 3 years for ages 21-29; for ages 30-65, options include high-risk HPV (hrHPV) testing alone every 5 years, hrHPV co-testing with cytology every 5 years, or cytology alone every 3 years. Primary hrHPV testing demonstrates superior sensitivity for detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3+ (CIN 3+). Guideline Protocol: HPV vaccination (Gardasil 9) recommended through age 26 (and shared clinical decision-making ages 27-45) to prevent over 90% of HPV-attributable cancers; smoking cessation (smoking impairs cervical clearance of high-risk HPV). Thresholds: ASCCP management guidelines dictate whether a patient requires immediate colposcopy or short-interval 1-year repeat testing based on immediate and 5-year calculated CIN 3+ risk.

solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: ASCCP management guidelines dictate whether a patient requires immediate colposcopy or short-interval 1-year repeat testing based on immediate and 5-year calculated CIN 3+ risk.

title: Crohn's Disease (Inflammatory Bowel Disease): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACG)
snippet: Guidelines recommend a 'Treat-to-Target' strategy aiming for deep mucosal healing, not just symptom resolution. For moderate-to-severe disease, anti-TNF biologics (Infliximab, Adalimumab) or anti-integrins (Vedolizumab) are first-line to induce and maintain remission. Systemic corticosteroids should be used strictly for acute flares and never for maintenance due to severe long-term toxicity. Guideline Protocol: Absolute smoking cessation (smoking doubles the risk of surgical resection and disease recurrence); screening for malnutrition and bone density loss; exclusive enteral nutrition (EEN) in severe pediatric cases. Thresholds: Surgical bowel resection is reserved for medication-refractory disease, strictures causing bowel obstruction, or fistulizing disease.

solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Surgical bowel resection is reserved for medication-refractory disease, strictures causing bowel obstruction, or fistulizing disease.

title: Ulcerative Colitis (Inflammatory Bowel Disease): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACG)
snippet: Unlike Crohn's, UC is limited to the mucosal layer of the colon. For mild-to-moderate UC, topical (rectal) and oral 5-aminosalicylates (5-ASA/Mesalamine) are first-line. For moderate-to-severe disease, targeted biologics (Infliximab, Vedolizumab) or JAK inhibitors (Tofacitinib) are recommended. Annual surveillance colonoscopy is required after 8 years of disease due to significantly elevated colorectal cancer risk. Guideline Protocol: Maintaining hydration during severe diarrheal flares; avoidance of NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) which can trigger disease flares; iron supplementation for chronic blood loss. Thresholds: Hospitalization indicated for acute severe ulcerative colitis (≥6 bloody bowel movements/day with systemic toxicity like fever or tachycardia).

title: Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AHA / ACC)
snippet: Diagnosis is established by a resting Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) ≤0.90. First-line therapy for intermittent claudication is Supervised Exercise Therapy (SET), which increases maximal walking distance by 100-150% (superior to pharmacotherapy). Antiplatelet therapy (Aspirin or Clopidogrel) and high-intensity statin therapy are mandatory to reduce the high risk of myocardial infarction and stroke in PAD patients. Guideline Protocol: Absolute smoking cessation (essential to prevent limb amputation); Supervised Exercise Therapy (treadmill walking to the point of moderate pain, resting, and repeating for 30-45 minutes, 3 times/week); strict foot care and daily inspections. Thresholds: Revascularization (endovascular or surgical bypass) is reserved for lifestyle-limiting claudication unresponsive to SET, or Critical Limb Ischemia (rest pain, non-healing ulcers).

solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Annual ABI assessment and clinical evaluation of walking distance capacity.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Revascularization (endovascular or surgical bypass) is reserved for lifestyle-limiting claudication unresponsive to SET, or Critical Limb Ischemia (rest pain, non-healing ulcers).

title: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (EULAR)
snippet: Hydroxychloroquine is recommended for all patients with SLE, unless contraindicated, as it improves survival, reduces flares, and prevents organ damage (Grade A). Glucocorticoids should be used at the lowest possible dose (target ≤7.5 mg/day of prednisone) and tapered as soon as possible. Belimumab (anti-BAFF) is approved for autoantibody-positive SLE with inadequate response to standard therapy. Guideline Protocol: Strict sun protection (broad-spectrum sunscreen SPF >50, UV-protective clothing) as UV light triggers systemic flares; cardiovascular risk management (SLE carries a significantly elevated risk of premature atherosclerosis); avoidance of sulfa-containing antibiotics. Thresholds: Target: Clinical remission (SLEDAI = 0) or Low Disease Activity (LLDAS) without reliance on chronic systemic steroids.

title: HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (CDC)
snippet: Daily oral TDF/FTC (Truvada) or TAF/FTC (Descovy) reduces the risk of getting HIV from sex by about 99% when taken consistently. Long-acting injectable Cabotegravir (Apretude) given every 2 months was shown in HPTN 083/084 trials to be superior to daily oral PrEP in preventing HIV acquisition, offering an option for those with adherence challenges. Guideline Protocol: Concurrent use of condoms to prevent other sexually transmitted infections (STIs) which PrEP does not cover; adherence counseling. Thresholds: PrEP must be discontinued immediately and converted to full antiretroviral therapy (ART) if an HIV test returns positive to prevent drug resistance.

title: Chronic Hepatitis C (HCV): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AASLD / IDSA)
snippet: Direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) such as Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir (Epclusa) or Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir (Mavyret) achieve Sustained Virologic Response (SVR) — considered a virologic cure — in >95% of patients across all genotypes after 8 to 12 weeks of oral therapy. Guideline Protocol: Absolute avoidance of alcohol (accelerates liver fibrosis); vaccination against Hepatitis A and B; weight management to prevent concurrent fatty liver disease. title: Sickle Cell Disease: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ASH)
snippet: Hydroxyurea is the primary disease-modifying therapy, strongly recommended for adults with ≥3 moderate-to-severe pain crises per year, demonstrating significant reductions in vaso-occlusive crises, acute chest syndrome, and mortality. Guideline Protocol: Aggressive daily hydration; avoidance of extreme temperatures (both cold and excessive heat); routine folic acid supplementation; ensuring complete pneumococcal and meningococcal vaccinations due to functional asplenia. title: Multiple Sclerosis (Relapsing-Remitting): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (OPERA I/II))
snippet: In relapsing MS, high-efficacy Disease Modifying Therapies (DMTs) like Ocrelizumab (anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody) demonstrate superior efficacy over older therapies (Interferon beta-1a), lowering annualized relapse rates by 46% and significantly reducing disability progression. title: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (CDC)
snippet: Empiric, broad-spectrum treatment should be initiated in sexually active young women experiencing lower abdominal pain if cervical motion tenderness or adnexal tenderness is present on exam. title: Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia (Jaundice): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAP)
snippet: The AAP provides age-in-hours specific nomograms for initiating phototherapy or exchange transfusion. Universal screening of Total Serum Bilirubin (TSB) or Transcutaneous Bilirubin (TcB) is recommended before hospital discharge. Phototherapy is highly effective at converting unconjugated bilirubin into water-soluble isomers for excretion, preventing bilirubin encephalopathy (kernicterus). Guideline Protocol: Frequent, exclusive breastfeeding (8-12 times per day) in the first days of life to promote bowel movements and enteral excretion of bilirubin; assessment by a lactation consultant to ensure adequate milk transfer. title: Acute Pancreatitis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACG)
snippet: Aggressive early intravenous hydration (250-500 mL/hr of lactated Ringer's) within the first 12-24 hours is most beneficial to prevent tissue necrosis. Guideline Protocol: Strict cessation of all alcohol consumption; early refeeding as tolerated by pain; ERCP intervention if concurrent acute cholangitis or biliary obstruction is present. snippet: Non-selective beta-blockers (NSBBs: Propranolol, Nadolol, Carvedilol) or Endoscopic Band Ligation (EBL) are recommended for primary prophylaxis of medium-to-large esophageal varices to prevent catastrophic bleeding. snippet: Intravenous Tenecteplase or Alteplase (tPA) is strongly recommended for eligible patients presenting within 3.0 to 4.5 hours of symptom onset. title: Adult Epilepsy & Seizure Disorders: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAN / AES)
snippet: Levetiracetam, Lamotrigine, and Zonisamide demonstrate Level A evidence for new-onset focal epilepsy in adults. Valproic acid remains highly effective for generalized epilepsy but carries severe teratogenic risks and is contraindicated in women of childbearing potential without strict contraception. Over 60-70% of patients achieve seizure freedom on monotherapy. Guideline Protocol: Strict sleep hygiene (sleep deprivation is the most common seizure trigger); avoidance of excessive alcohol and illicit stimulants; driving restriction compliance per local laws (usually 3-6 months seizure-free). snippet: The 'Hour-1 Bundle' is critical for mortality reduction: 1) Measure lactate, 2) Obtain blood cultures before antibiotics, 3) Administer broad-spectrum IV antibiotics, 4) Begin rapid 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid fluid resuscitation for hypotension or lactate ≥4 mmol/L, 5) Apply vasopressors (Norepinephrine first-line) if hypotensive during/after fluids. title: Active Tuberculosis (TB): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ATS / CDC / IDSA)
snippet: Standard treatment for drug-susceptible active TB requires a 4-drug intensive phase for 2 months (Isoniazid [INH], Rifampin [RIF], Pyrazinamide [PZA], Ethambutol [EMB]), followed by a 2-drug continuation phase for 4 months (INH and RIF). title: Syphilis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (CDC)
snippet: Parenteral Penicillin G is the only therapy with documented efficacy across all stages of syphilis. Primary, secondary, and early latent syphilis require a single dose of Benzathine penicillin G (2.4 million units IM). Late latent or unknown duration requires 3 doses spaced 1 week apart. Neurosyphilis requires aqueous crystalline penicillin G IV for 10-14 days. Doxycycline is an alternative for penicillin-allergic non-pregnant patients. Guideline Protocol: Abstinence from sexual contact until the chancre/lesions are completely healed and at least 7 days post-treatment; mandatory partner notification and treatment; concurrent HIV testing. Thresholds: Successful treatment is defined as a fourfold (two-dilution) decline in the RPR or VDRL titer (e.g., from 1:32 to 1:8) by 6-12 months.

title: Bacterial Meningitis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (IDSA)
snippet: Empiric antimicrobial therapy (IV Ceftriaxone + IV Vancomycin; add Ampicillin if >50 years or immunocompromised for Listeria coverage) must be initiated immediately, ideally within 60 minutes of presentation. title: Hyperthyroidism & Graves' Disease: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ATA)
snippet: Methimazole (MMI) is the preferred first-line antithyroid drug over Propylthiouracil (PTU) due to PTU's risk of severe hepatotoxicity (except during the first trimester of pregnancy where PTU is preferred). title: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (KDIGO)
snippet: AKI is defined by an increase in serum creatinine by ≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours, or ≥1.5x baseline within 7 days, or urine output <0.5 mL/kg/hr for 6 hours. title: Parkinson's Disease: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (MDS)
snippet: Levodopa/Carbidopa remains the most effective symptomatic treatment for motor symptoms (bradykinesia, rigidity). title: Fibromyalgia: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACR / EULAR)
snippet: Non-pharmacological therapies (specifically graded aerobic exercise) have the highest evidence level (Grade A) and are the only universally recommended first-line therapy. Strong recommendations strictly oppose the use of opioids and strong analgesics, which worsen central sensitization and hyperalgesia. Guideline Protocol: Graded, low-impact aerobic exercise (aquatic therapy, walking, cycling); Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to reduce pain catastrophizing; mindfulness and sleep hygiene optimization. title: Anaphylaxis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAAAI / ACAAI / WAO)
snippet: Epinephrine (intramuscular into the anterolateral thigh) is the only first-line treatment for anaphylaxis. Antihistamines (H1/H2 blockers) and corticosteroids are second-line adjunctive therapies that do not treat the life-threatening respiratory or cardiovascular compromise of anaphylaxis and must never delay epinephrine administration. A second dose of epinephrine may be required in 5-15 minutes if symptoms do not improve. Guideline Protocol: Immediate removal of the trigger if possible (e.g., stopping an IV drug infusion, removing a stinger); place patient in a supine position with legs elevated (unless causing respiratory distress) to prevent empty vena cava syndrome. Thresholds: Anaphylaxis is diagnosed by acute onset involving skin/mucosal tissue PLUS either respiratory compromise, reduced blood pressure, or severe gastrointestinal symptoms.

title: Acute Diverticulitis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AGA)
snippet: For acute uncomplicated diverticulitis in immunocompetent patients, routine use of antibiotics is no longer recommended, as RCTs show no improvement in recovery time or prevention of complications (Grade: Conditional). Management relies on clear liquid diet and pain control. Antibiotics (e.g., Ciprofloxacin + Metronidazole) are reserved for complicated cases (abscess, perforation) or high-risk patients. Guideline Protocol: Clear liquid diet for 2-3 days during acute flares, advancing to a low-fiber diet as symptoms resolve; once fully recovered, transition to a high-fiber diet to prevent recurrence. Thresholds: CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast is the imaging modality of choice to distinguish uncomplicated from complicated disease (Hinchey classification).

title: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACR)
snippet: GCA is a medical emergency due to the high risk of irreversible blindness. High-dose systemic glucocorticoids (Prednisone 40-60 mg/day; IV Methylprednisolone if visual symptoms are present) must be started immediately upon clinical suspicion, before biopsy confirmation. Tocilizumab (IL-6 receptor antagonist) combined with a steroid taper is strongly recommended over steroids alone to reduce cumulative steroid toxicity and flares. Guideline Protocol: Given high-dose steroid requirements: calcium and vitamin D supplementation; bone density monitoring; blood glucose monitoring. Thresholds: Diagnosis supported by new-onset localized headache, jaw claudication, visual symptoms, and elevated ESR >50 mm/hr in adults >50 years old.

title: Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma (POAG): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAO)
snippet: Lowering intraocular pressure (IOP) is the only proven method to slow visual field loss. Topical prostaglandin analogs (Latanoprost, Bimatoprost) are the preferred first-line medical therapy due to once-daily dosing and high efficacy (lowering IOP by 25-33%). Selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) is equally effective as a first-line alternative to eye drops (LiGHT Trial, The Lancet). Guideline Protocol: Proper eye drop administration technique (nasolacrimal occlusion for 1-2 minutes after instillation to minimize systemic absorption and side effects); avoidance of inverted yoga positions which spike IOP. Thresholds: Target IOP is typically set 20-30% below the pre-treatment baseline pressure, adjusted dynamically based on visual field progression.

title: Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAO & NEJM (AREDS2))
snippet: For intermediate dry AMD, AREDS2 antioxidant vitamin formulation (Vitamin C, E, Lutein, Zeaxanthin, Zinc, Copper) reduces the 5-year risk of progression to advanced AMD by 25%. For advanced 'wet' (neovascular) AMD, intravitreal anti-VEGF injections (Bevacizumab, Ranibizumab, Aflibercept) are the standard of care, preventing severe vision loss in over 90% of patients and improving vision in 30%. Guideline Protocol: Absolute smoking cessation (smoking doubles AMD risk and accelerates progression); UV protection (sunglasses); diet rich in green leafy vegetables (lutein) and omega-3 fatty acids. Thresholds: Conversion from 'dry' to 'wet' AMD is marked by new fluid or hemorrhage under the retina on OCT, requiring immediate anti-VEGF therapy.

title: Bell's Palsy (Idiopathic Facial Paralysis): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAN)
snippet: Oral corticosteroids (e.g., Prednisone 60 mg/day for 5 days, then tapered) initiated within 72 hours of symptom onset significantly increase the probability of complete facial nerve recovery (Grade A). The addition of antiviral therapy (valacyclovir) provides only modest, conditional benefit for severe cases (House-Brackmann grade V-VI) but should not be used as monotherapy. Guideline Protocol: Eye protection is paramount: rigorous use of artificial tears during the day, lubricating ointment at night, and physically taping the affected eyelid shut during sleep to prevent corneal abrasions/ulceration. Thresholds: If facial paralysis spares the forehead (i.e., the patient can wrinkle their forehead normally on the paralyzed side), Bell's palsy is excluded, and acute stroke must be evaluated immediately.

title: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAOS)
snippet: First-line conservative management includes neutral-angle wrist splinting (worn primarily at night) and local corticosteroid injections, which provide robust short-to-medium term relief (Grade Strong). Oral NSAIDs, diuretics, and gabapentin are not recommended. For patients with severe nerve compression (muscle atrophy) or those failing conservative therapy, surgical carpal tunnel release provides excellent long-term outcomes. Guideline Protocol: Ergonomic workplace modifications (keyboard/mouse alignment); nocturnal volar wrist splinting; nerve gliding exercises. Thresholds: Thenar atrophy (wasting of the thumb base muscle) or persistent sensory loss mandates urgent surgical evaluation to prevent irreversible nerve death.

title: Mild Traumatic Brain Injury (Concussion): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (CDC & AAN)
snippet: Routine neuroimaging (CT/MRI) is NOT recommended for mild TBI without red-flag symptoms, to avoid unnecessary radiation exposure (Grade A). Complete physical and cognitive rest beyond 2-3 days is discouraged; early, gradually escalating light aerobic activity speeds recovery compared to strict rest (cocooning). Guideline Protocol: Graduated Return-to-Learn and Return-to-Play protocols; strict avoidance of any activity with a risk of secondary head impact until fully cleared; optimization of sleep; limitation of screen time only if it provokes symptoms. Thresholds: Clearance for contact sports requires the patient to be completely asymptomatic at rest and during maximal physical exertion without the use of pain medications.

title: Allergic Rhinitis (Hay Fever): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAAI / ACAAI)
snippet: Intranasal corticosteroids (INCS: Fluticasone, Budesonide) are the most effective monotherapy for all symptoms of allergic rhinitis (sneezing, congestion, itching) and are strongly recommended as first-line treatment for moderate-to-severe disease. Oral second-generation antihistamines (Cetirizine, Loratadine) are effective for mild, episodic symptoms but do not relieve severe nasal congestion. First-generation antihistamines (Diphenhydramine) should be avoided due to sedation and anticholinergic side effects. Guideline Protocol: Allergen avoidance (HEPA air filters, washing bedding in hot water for dust mites, keeping windows closed during high pollen seasons); nasal saline irrigation (Neti pot) with distilled/boiled water. Thresholds: Allergen immunotherapy (subcutaneous shots or sublingual tablets) is indicated for patients with severe disease refractory to pharmacotherapy.

title: Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (Hives): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (EAACI / WAO)
snippet: Defined as hives occurring most days for >6 weeks. First-line therapy is regular-dosed modern second-generation H1-antihistamines (Cetirizine, Fexofenadine). If refractory to high-dose antihistamines, Omalizumab (anti-IgE biologic) is the recommended add-on therapy. Guideline Protocol: Avoidance of exacerbating factors (NSAIDs, tight clothing, extreme heat or cold, stress); keeping a symptom diary to track flares using the Urticaria Activity Score (UAS7). title: Acne Vulgaris: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAD)
snippet: Topical retinoids (Adapalene, Tretinoin) are the foundation of acne therapy, targeting microcomedone formation. title: Ectopic Pregnancy: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACOG)
snippet: Diagnosis requires transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) and serial quantitative beta-hCG measurements. If a patient is hemodynamically stable, willing to comply with post-treatment follow-up, and meets criteria (mass <3-4 cm, no fetal cardiac activity), medical management with intramuscular Methotrexate is safe and effective. Hemodynamic instability or evidence of rupture mandates immediate surgical intervention (laparoscopy/salpingectomy). Thresholds: hCG levels must be monitored weekly until they reach non-pregnant levels (<5 mIU/mL).

solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Serial quantitative hCG testing on Days 4 and 7 post-Methotrexate. A decrease of ≥15% between Day 4 and Day 7 indicates successful treatment; if <15%, a second dose or surgery is required.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: hCG levels must be monitored weekly until they reach non-pregnant levels (<5 mIU/mL).

title: Postmenopausal Bleeding & Endometrial Hyperplasia: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (ACOG)
snippet: Any postmenopausal bleeding requires immediate investigation to rule out endometrial cancer (present in ~10% of cases). Initial evaluation options are transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) or endometrial biopsy. An endometrial thickness of ≤4 mm on TVUS carries a >99% negative predictive value for endometrial cancer, and observation is reasonable. Thickness >4 mm requires endometrial tissue sampling. Guideline Protocol: Weight management (obesity is a primary risk factor for estrogen-driven endometrial hyperplasia). Thresholds: Endometrial hyperplasia with atypia carries a high risk of concurrent or future cancer and is typically managed with hysterectomy; hyperplasia without atypia is managed with progestin therapy (e.g., Levonorgestrel IUD).

title: Erectile Dysfunction (ED): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AUA)
snippet: ED is a recognized early clinical marker for underlying Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (ASCVD); symptoms of ED often precede coronary events by 3-5 years. Phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE5) inhibitors (Sildenafil, Tadalafil) are first-line oral therapy. PDE5 inhibitors are absolutely contraindicated in patients taking nitrates (due to severe refractory hypotension) and must be used with caution with alpha-blockers. Guideline Protocol: Cardiovascular risk reduction: strict smoking cessation, weight loss, Mediterranean diet, and aerobic exercise (proven to improve endothelial function and ED severity); psychological counseling for performance anxiety. Thresholds: If oral PDE5 inhibitors fail or are contraindicated, intracavernosal injections (Alprostadil), vacuum erection devices, or surgical penile prostheses are indicated.

title: Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (AAN)
snippet: First-line evaluation must include checking serum ferritin, as brain iron deficiency is a primary driver of RLS. If ferritin is <75 ng/mL, iron supplementation is the first-line therapy. For pharmacological symptom control, alpha-2-delta ligands (Pregabalin, Gabapentin enacarbil) are preferred. Dopamine agonists (Pramipexole, Ropinirole) are effective but carry a high risk of 'augmentation' (paradoxical worsening of symptoms over time). Guideline Protocol: Avoidance of caffeine, alcohol, and nicotine near bedtime; moderate aerobic exercise; pneumatic compression devices; review of current medications (antidepressants like SSRIs/SNRIs and antihistamines strongly exacerbate RLS). Thresholds: Diagnosis requires URGE criteria: Urge to move legs, Rest worsens symptoms, Getting up/movement relieves symptoms, Evening/nighttime worsening.

title: Acute Appendicitis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (WSES)
snippet: Laparoscopic appendectomy remains the gold standard treatment for acute appendicitis. While non-operative management (antibiotics alone) can be successful in selected patients with uncomplicated appendicitis, there is a recurrence rate of up to 39% at 5 years (CODA trial). Surgery is mandatory for complicated appendicitis (perforation, peritonitis, abscess). Guideline Protocol: Immediate NPO (nothing by mouth) status in the emergency department; IV fluid resuscitation and analgesia. Thresholds: CT scan of the abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast is the most accurate imaging modality in adults; Ultrasound is preferred in children and pregnant women to avoid radiation.

title: Hyperkalemia (Elevated Blood Potassium): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (KDIGO)
snippet: Severe hyperkalemia (≥6.5 mEq/L) or any hyperkalemia with ECG changes (peaked T waves, widened QRS) is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate myocardial stabilization with IV Calcium Gluconate (or Calcium Chloride). This must be followed by intracellular potassium-shifting agents (IV Insulin with Dextrose, Albuterol) and eventually potassium-removing agents (Loop diuretics, GI cation binders like Patiromer, or emergent Hemodialysis). Guideline Protocol: Strict low-potassium diet restriction; immediate cessation of all potassium-sparing medications (ACEi/ARBs, MRAs like Spironolactone, NSAIDs). Thresholds: Emergent hemodialysis is indicated for hyperkalemia refractory to medical management or in the setting of severe oliguric renal failure.

title: Aortic Valve Stenosis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (PARTNER 3))
snippet: In 1,000 low-risk patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve was superior to surgical replacement with respect to composite death, stroke, or rehospitalization at 1 year (8.5% vs 15.1%; difference -7.1 percentage points; 95% CI -10.8 to -3.5; p<0.001 for noninferiority, p=0.001 for superiority). Standard therapy requires echocardiographic surveillance and valve intervention once AVA <1.0 cm2 or mean gradient >=40 mmHg with symptoms. Guideline Protocol: Avoidance of competitive vigorous exertion once severe; structured low-intensity cardiac conditioning; strict systolic blood pressure control without sudden vasodilation. Thresholds: Aortic valve area (AVA) < 1.0 cm² or mean gradient ≥ 40 mmHg, peak velocity ≥ 4.0 m/s triggers valve team evaluation.

title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HCM): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (The Lancet (EXPLORER-HCM))
snippet: In 251 patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the cardiac myosin inhibitor mavacamten significantly increased peak oxygen consumption (pVO2) and reduced LVOT gradient by 36 mmHg vs placebo (p<0.0001). 37% of mavacamten-treated patients met the primary composite endpoint vs 17% in placebo. First-line therapy includes non-vasodilating beta-blockers or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers. Guideline Protocol: Adequate daily hydration (avoid dehydration/hypovolemia); avoidance of intense competitive athletics or sudden burst training; genetic counseling for first-degree relatives. Thresholds: LV wall thickness ≥ 30 mm, unexplained syncope, or family history of sudden death mandates ICD risk score evaluation.

title: Infective Endocarditis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Circulation (AHA))
snippet: AHA/ESC guidelines mandate modified Duke Criteria for diagnostic confirmation (positive blood cultures across multiple bottles and transesophageal echocardiographic demonstration of oscillating vegetation or abscess). Intravenous bactericidal antibiotic therapy tailored to organism (viridans streptococci, S. aureus, Enterococcus) for 4-6 weeks is required. Early surgical valve replacement is indicated for heart failure, fungal/resistant infection, or persistent large mobile vegetations (>10 mm) with recurrent embolization. Guideline Protocol: Meticulous oral dental hygiene; prompt eradication of skin/catheter infection sources; antibiotic prophylaxis before dental procedures only in high-risk cardiac cohorts. Thresholds: Vegetation size > 10 mm on valve leaflet or severe acute valvular regurgitation triggers urgent surgical evaluation.

title: Acute Pericarditis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM (ICAP))
snippet: In 240 patients with acute pericarditis, the addition of weight-adjusted colchicine (0.5 mg daily or BID for 3 months) to standard NSAID therapy reduced recurrence rates from 37.5% to 16.7% (relative risk reduction 56%; number needed to treat = 5; p<0.001) and reduced symptom persistence at 72 hours (19.2% vs 40.0%; p=0.001). Diagnostic criteria require at least 2 of 4: pleuritic chest pain improved by leaning forward, pericardial friction rub, PR depression/diffuse ST elevation on ECG, and new/worsening pericardial effusion. Guideline Protocol: Exercise restriction (avoid strenuous activity and competitive sports) until complete resolution of symptoms and normalization of CRP/ESR. Thresholds: Effusion size > 20 mm on echo, hemodynamic compromise (pulsus paradoxus > 10 mmHg), or tamponade mandates emergent pericardiocentesis.

title: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm (AAA): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg (ESVS))
snippet: ESVS and SVS guidelines recommend ultrasound screening for men aged 65-75 with any smoking history. Threshold for elective repair (EVAR or open surgical repair) is an aneurysm diameter >= 5.5 cm in men, >= 5.0 cm in women, or rapid expansion >= 1.0 cm/year. Intensive medical management includes smoking cessation (the strongest modifiable risk factor for expansion and rupture), high-intensity statin therapy, and antiplatelet therapy for systemic atherosclerotic risk reduction. Guideline Protocol: Immediate, complete tobacco cessation; avoidance of extreme isometric heavy weightlifting; moderate systolic BP control (<130/80 mmHg). Thresholds: Aortic diameter ≥ 5.5 cm in men or ≥ 5.0 cm in women triggers vascular surgical consultation for repair.

title: Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension (nOH): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Clin Auton Res (AAS/EFNS))
snippet: Diagnostic consensus defines orthostatic hypotension as a sustained reduction of systolic blood pressure of at least 20 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure of at least 10 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing or head-up tilt. In neurogenic forms (Parkinson's, MSA, diabetic autonomic neuropathy), blunted reflex tachycardia (ratio of delta HR to delta SBP <0.5 bpm/mmHg) reflects sympathetic failure. Pharmacotherapy includes droxidopa, midodrine, or fludrocortisone titrated against supine hypertension. Guideline Protocol: Bolus water drinking (500 mL water 30 min before rising); dietary sodium expansion (6-10 g salt/day unless contraindicated); thigh-high compression stockings (30-40 mmHg); abdominal binder. Thresholds: Standing systolic BP maintained > 90 mmHg without symptoms while keeping supine nocturnal BP < 180/110 mmHg.

title: Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Heart Rhythm (HRS))
snippet: HRS consensus criteria require a sustained heart rate increase of >= 30 bpm (or >= 40 bpm in individuals aged 12-19) within 10 minutes of standing or tilt-table testing, in the absence of orthostatic hypotension, accompanied by chronic orthostatic symptoms for >= 3 months. First-line therapy centers on non-pharmacological intravascular volume expansion: 2-3 L oral fluids daily, 8-10 g sodium daily, structured recumbent/rowing exercise training. Pharmacologic adjuncts include fludrocortisone, propranolol/bisoprolol, pyridostigmine, and midodrine. Guideline Protocol: High fluid intake (2.5-3.0 L/day) and high sodium intake (8-10 g/day); waist-high compression garments (20-30 mmHg); Levine semi-recumbent progressive aerobic exercise protocol. Thresholds: Postural heart rate increase < 30 bpm during sustained standing indicates therapeutic stabilization.

title: Raynaud's Phenomenon: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (NEJM Review)
snippet: Primary Raynaud's (idiopathic vasospasm) is distinguished from secondary Raynaud's (underlying connective tissue disease such as systemic sclerosis, SLE) by normal nailfold capillaroscopy, symmetric attacks, absence of digital ulceration/necrosis, and negative antinuclear antibody (ANA) serology. First-line pharmacotherapy consists of dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (nifedipine 30-60 mg daily or amlodipine 5-10 mg daily), reducing attack frequency by 33% and severity by 35% in meta-analyses. Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (sildenafil) are effective for refractory symptoms or digital ulcers. Guideline Protocol: Core and extremity cold avoidance (layering, thermal mittens, hand warmers); avoidance of emotional stress triggers; complete avoidance of nicotine/smoking and sympathomimetic decongestants. Thresholds: Digital tissue loss, persistent cyanosis >2 hours, or nailfold capillary drop-out mandates secondary autoimmune disease workup.

title: Sick Sinus Syndrome (Bradycardia-Tachycardia): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Circulation (ACC/AHA/HRS))
snippet: ACC/AHA/HRS guidelines establish that permanent pacemaker implantation (dual-chamber DDDR preferred over single-chamber) is a Class I recommendation for documented symptomatic sinus node dysfunction (sinus pauses >3 seconds, chronotropic incompetence, or symptomatic bradycardia). In tachycardia-bradycardia syndrome, pacing prevents post-conversion pauses, enabling safe use of AV-nodal blocking agents (beta-blockers) and anticoagulation for concurrent atrial fibrillation. Guideline Protocol: Audit and discontinuation of non-essential negative chronotropic medications (beta-blockers, non-DHP CCBs, antiarrhythmics, digoxin); avoidance of vagal triggers. title: Supraventricular Tachycardia (AVNRT / AVRT): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Circulation (ACC/AHA/HRS))
snippet: Clinical guidelines recommend modified Valsalva maneuver (REVERT protocol: 15-second strain at 40 mmHg followed by immediate supine repositioning and 45-degree passive leg elevation for 15 seconds) as first-line bedside therapy, achieving 43% cardioversion vs 17% standard Valsalva (p<0.0001). Catheter ablation is Class I curative therapy with >95% success and <1% major complication rate. title: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Eur Heart J (ESC/ERS))
snippet: Hemodynamic definition updated to mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) > 20 mmHg with pulmonary capillary wedge pressure <= 15 mmHg and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) > 2 Wood units. Initial upfront oral dual combination therapy (ERA + PDE5i: macitentan/tadalafil or ambrisentan/tadalafil) demonstrated significant reduction in clinical failure events (AMBITION trial, HR 0.50, p<0.001). Parenteral prostacyclin analogues (epoprostenol) are mandatory for high-risk patients. Guideline Protocol: Supervised pulmonary rehabilitation; sodium restriction (<2,000 mg/day) for right ventricular volume overload; annual influenza/pneumococcal/COVID vaccinations; pregnancy avoidance due to high maternal mortality. title: Bronchiectasis (Non-Cystic Fibrosis): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Eur Respir J (ERS))
snippet: Diagnostic confirmation requires high-resolution CT (HRCT) demonstrating bronchoarterial ratio > 1.0 (signet-ring sign) and lack of bronchial tapering. title: Acute Bronchitis: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Cochrane Database Syst Rev)
snippet: Over 90% of acute bronchitis cases in immunocompetent adults are caused by respiratory viruses (rhinovirus, coronavirus, influenza, RSV, parainfluenza). snippet: Diagnostic attribution per Helsinki criteria requires documented occupational latency (typically >15-20 years from first exposure), high-resolution CT demonstration of bilateral basilar interstitial fibrosis, subpleural curvilinear lines, dot-like opacities, and pleural plaques. title: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Diabetes Care (ADA/EASD))

snippet: Primary adrenal insufficiency results from autoimmune destruction of the adrenal cortex (80-90% of cases in developed nations), leading to deficient glucocorticoid, mineralocorticoid, and adrenal androgen production. title: Cushing's Syndrome (Hypercortisolism): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (J Clin Endocrinol Metab)
snippet: Endogenous hypercortisolism causes central obesity, proximal muscle weakness, wide violaceous striae (>1 cm), facial plethora, osteopenia, and severe neuropsychiatric symptoms. Diagnosis requires at least two concordant first-line screening tests: 24-hour urinary free cortisol (UFC >3x ULN), late-night salivary cortisol (>145 ng/dL on 2 separate evenings), or overnight 1-mg dexamethasone suppression test (serum cortisol > 1.8 mcg/dL at 8 AM). Cushing disease (ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma, 70%) is treated with transsphenoidal adenomectomy; adrenal adenomas require laparoscopic adrenalectomy. Steroidogenesis inhibitors (ketoconazole, metyrapone, osilodrostat) serve as bridge or adjuvant medical therapy. Guideline Protocol: Dietary sodium restriction (<2,000 mg/day) to manage cortisol-mediated hypertension; high-protein diet to counter catabolic muscle wasting; falls prevention for fragile bones. Thresholds: Post-dexamethasone cortisol > 1.8 mcg/dL indicates lack of physiological suppression.

title: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (J Bone Miner Res)
snippet: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is characterized by hypercalcemia driven by autonomously elevated or inappropriately normal intact parathyroid hormone (PTH), primarily caused by a single benign parathyroid adenoma (85%). Classic clinical manifestations include nephrolithiasis, cortical bone resorption (osteoporosis at the distal 1/3 radius), constipation, and cognitive impairment. Parathyroidectomy provides definitive surgical cure with >95% success. Surgical criteria for asymptomatic patients include: serum calcium > 1.0 mg/dL above normal ULN, T-score ≤ -2.5 at lumbar spine, hip, or 1/3 radius, age < 50 years, eGFR < 60 mL/min, or 24-hour urinary calcium > 250 mg (women) / 300 mg (men). Guideline Protocol: Adequate daily oral hydration (2-3 liters water daily) to reduce calcium nephrolithiasis risk; maintain moderate dietary calcium intake (1,000 mg/day; calcium restriction triggers higher PTH output); avoid thiazide diuretics and lithium. Thresholds: Serum calcium > 1.0 mg/dL above ULN or T-score ≤ -2.5 at forearm/spine/hip meets surgical indication.

title: Hypoparathyroidism: Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Eur J Endocrinol)
snippet: Hypoparathyroidism results in hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and hypercalciuria due to absent or inadequate PTH secretion (most commonly iatrogenic after total thyroidectomy or neck dissection). Neuromuscular irritability manifests as perioral numbness, paresthesias, Chvostek's/Trousseau's signs, carpopedal spasms, and laryngospasm. Standard therapy relies on oral calcium carbonate/citrate (1,000-3,000 mg/day elemental) combined with active vitamin D metabolites (calcitriol 0.25-2.0 mcg/day). The therapeutic objective is maintaining serum albumin-adjusted calcium in the low-normal range (8.0-8.5 mg/dL) while avoiding hypercalciuria (24-hr urine calcium < 300 mg/day) to prevent nephrocalcinosis and renal failure. Guideline Protocol: Dietary phosphate restriction (limit processed colas, preserved cheeses); split calcium supplement dosing across 3-4 meals to maximize gut absorption. Thresholds: Target corrected calcium 8.0-8.5 mg/dL; keep calcium-phosphate product < 55 mg²/dL² to avoid ectopic tissue calcification.

title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia (HeFH): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Eur Heart J)
snippet: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) is a dominant monogenic disorder (prevalence ~1:250) caused by mutations in LDLR, APOB, or PCSK9, leading to lifelong severe LDL-C elevation (>190 mg/dL in adults) and a >10-fold increased lifetime risk of premature coronary artery disease. Dutch Lipid Clinic Network criteria score clinical history, tendon xanthomas, and LDL-C levels. First-line therapy mandates high-intensity statin therapy (atorvastatin 80 mg or rosuvastatin 40 mg) combined early with ezetimibe 10 mg (adds ~24% reduction), and PCSK9 monoclonal antibodies (evolocumab or alirocumab; adds ~50-60% reduction, FOURIER and ODYSSEY OUTCOMES trials) to achieve LDL-C targets (<55 mg/dL for secondary prevention; <70 mg/dL for primary prevention). Guideline Protocol: Heart-healthy Mediterranean diet low in saturated fats (<7% daily calories) and trans fats; avoidance of smoking; cascade genetic testing for all first-degree relatives. Thresholds: LDL-C ≥ 190 mg/dL in untreated adults or ≥ 155 mg/dL in untreated children strongly suggests HeFH; treatment target < 55 mg/dL if established ASCVD.
