title: Calcium Oxalate Nephrolithiasis (Hypercalciuria & Hypocitraturia): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Journal of Urology)
snippet: Calcium oxalate accounts for ~75-80% of all nephrolithiasis, radiopaque on X-ray/CT. Guideline Protocol: High fluid intake producing >=2.5 liters of urine daily (drink a glass of water every 2-3 hours and before sleep); DO NOT RESTRICT DIETARY CALCIUM (consume calcium WITH meals to bind dietary oxalate in the gut); limit high-oxalate foods (spinach, almonds, rhubarb, beets, dark chocolate); reduce animal protein and sodium intake. Thresholds: Radiopaque calcium oxalate monohydrate (dumbbell/oval) or dihydrate (envelope/bipyramidal) crystals on urinalysis or stone spectrometry.

patient_plain_language: The most common type of kidney stone (accounting for 80% of stones). Calcium binds with oxalate in your urine, crystallizing into sharp, jagged stones that lodge in your kidney tubes. Counterintuitively, cutting calcium from your diet makes stones WORSE because dietary calcium is needed in your gut to trap oxalate and flush it out. Drinking 3 liters of water daily and taking potassium citrate or a thiazide pill prevents new stones.

title: Uric Acid Nephrolithiasis (Radiolucent Stones & Alkalinization): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (European Urology)
snippet: Uric acid stones (~10% of stones) are INVISIBLE ON STANDARD X-RAY (RADIOLUCENT) but readily detected on non-contrast CT. ORAL CHEMOLYSIS (URINARY ALKALINIZATION WITH POTASSIUM CITRATE targeting urine pH 6.5-7.0) COMPLETELY DISSOLVES EXISTING URIC ACID STONES without requiring surgery. patient_plain_language: Kidney stones made of crystallized uric acid. Unlike calcium stones, uric acid stones are completely invisible on regular X-rays (radiolucent). They form almost exclusively because your urine is too acidic (pH below 5.5). The most remarkable fact about these stones is that they can be completely dissolved like sugar in hot tea simply by taking potassium citrate powder to make your urine alkaline (pH 6.5 to 7.0), completely avoiding surgery.

disease: Struvite Infection Stones (Triple Phosphate Staghorn Calculi)
title: Struvite Infection Stones (Triple Phosphate Staghorn Calculi): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Journal of Urology)
keywords: struvite infection stones (triple phosphate staghorn calculi)
snippet: Struvite stones (magnesium ammonium phosphate / triple phosphate) form EXCLUSIVELY in the presence of UREASE-PRODUCING BACTERIA (Proteus mirabilis, Klebsiella, Morganella, Pseudomonas). Bacterial urease hydrolyzes urea into ammonia and carbon dioxide, driving urine pH >7.2-8.0 and precipitating struvite and carbonate apatite. Struvite stones form massive branching 'staghorn calculi' that fill the entire renal pelvis. COMPLETE SURGICAL REMOVAL (PERCUTANEOUS NEPHROLITHOTOMY / PCNL) COMBINED WITH CULTURE-SPECIFIC ANTIBIOTICS IS MANDATORY; residual fragments inevitably cause fatal sepsis. Guideline Protocol: COMPLETE SURGICAL STONE CLEARANCE; culture-directed antibiotics; high fluid intake; treatment of predisposing anatomic factors (neurogenic bladder, indwelling catheters, urinary diversions); Acetohydroxamic acid (AHA - urease inhibitor) for non-surgical candidates. Thresholds: Presence of branching staghorn calculus filling >=1 calyx and renal pelvis on CT, associated with alkaline urine pH >7.2 and urease-positive bacteriuria.

patient_plain_language: Dangerous 'infection stones' that grow rapidly into giant branching antlers (staghorn stones) that fill your entire kidney plumbing system. They form exclusively when certain bacteria (like Proteus) produce an enzyme called urease, turning your urine strongly alkaline and creating magnesium-ammonium-phosphate crystals. Because the stone is literally made of living bacteria, antibiotics cannot penetrate it; keyhole surgery (PCNL) through your back to remove every last grain of stone is required to prevent life-threatening blood infections.

Guideline Protocol: Dietary elimination of bladder irritants (the '4 Cs': Coffee, Carbonated beverages, Citrus fruits, and Chili/spicy foods, plus alcohol and artificial sweeteners); pelvic floor physical therapy focused on downtraining and myofascial trigger point release; AVOID KEGEL EXERCISES (Kegels tighten hypertonic pelvic muscles, exacerbating agony); stress reduction. Avoiding acidic foods (coffee, citrus, tomatoes), doing relaxing pelvic floor physical therapy (never Kegel tightening), and taking bladder-protective pills brings lasting relief.

title: Anti-Glomerular Basement Membrane Disease (Goodpasture Syndrome): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Kidney International)
snippet: Autoantibodies directed against the non-collagenous domain of the alpha-3 chain of Type IV collagen [alpha3(IV)NC1] cause necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis and alveolar hemorrhage (Goodpasture triad: RPGN, pulmonary hemorrhage, anti-GBM antibodies). Dialysis independence is achieved in >80% if treated before serum creatinine >5.7 mg/dL or anuria. Guideline Protocol: IMMEDIATE INITIATION OF PLASMAPHERESIS AND CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE (hours count; treatment must NOT wait for renal biopsy confirmation if anti-GBM serology is strongly positive); absolute smoking cessation (tobacco smoke increases pulmonary capillary permeability, triggering catastrophic diffuse alveolar hemorrhage). Thresholds: Linear IgG deposition along the glomerular basement membrane on direct immunofluorescence of renal biopsy, with circulating Anti-GBM antibodies by ELISA.

It causes rapid kidney failure within days and can cause you to cough up blood. Immediate blood filtering (plasmapheresis) to wash out the antibodies, combined with strong immune-calming pills, preserves your kidneys and saves your life if started immediately.

title: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (GPA / Wegener's PR3-ANCA): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (New England Journal of Medicine)
snippet: GPA is a necrotizing granulomatous small-vessel vasculitis associated with PR3-ANCA (c-ANCA in 80-90%), causing destructive upper airway lesions (saddle nose deformity, subglottic stenosis), cavitary lung nodules, and crescentic glomerulonephritis. The RAVE trial established RITUXIMAB (375 mg/m2 weekly x 4) as non-inferior to cyclophosphamide for induction and superior for relapsing disease. The landmark ADVOCATE trial (n=330) proved that oral Complement C5a Receptor Antagonist AVACOPAN (30 mg BID) replaced high-dose glucocorticoids, achieving superior sustained remission at week 52 (65.7% vs 54.9%; p=0.007) with 60% lower steroid toxicity. Guideline Protocol: Targeted B-cell depletion and complement inhibition to eliminate toxic glucocorticoid exposure; ENT saline rinses; trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim) prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (MANDATORY during rituximab/cyclophosphamide therapy); monitor for sinus infections. Thresholds: Cavitary lung lesions on CT, pauci-immune necrotizing crescentic GN on biopsy, and high-titer PR3-ANCA (c-ANCA).

patient_plain_language: An autoimmune condition where antibodies (PR3-ANCA) inflame and destroy small blood vessels, particularly in your nose, sinuses, lungs, and kidneys. It can cause chronic bloody nasal crusts, a collapsed nasal bridge ('saddle nose'), lung cavities, and kidney inflammation. Modern treatment uses targeted B-cell clearing infusions (Rituximab) and a breakthrough steroid-sparing pill (Avacopan) that shields your kidneys without the severe side effects of high-dose prednisone.

title: Microscopic Polyangiitis (MPA - MPO-ANCA / p-ANCA): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (New England Journal of Medicine)
snippet: Unlike GPA, MPA is NON-GRANULOMATOUS, lacks destructive sinus/upper airway involvement, and is predominantly associated with MPO-ANCA (perinuclear p-ANCA in 70-85%). Presents with rapidly progressive necrotizing glomerulonephritis and alveolar hemorrhage. The landmark PEXIVAS trial (n=704) proved that routine plasma exchange did NOT reduce death or ESRD in severe ANCA vasculitis, and established that a REDUCED-DOSE GLUCOCORTICOID PROTOCOL was non-inferior to high-dose steroids for remission while cutting serious infections by 31% (hazard ratio 0.69; p=0.02). Guideline Protocol: Reduced-dose oral corticosteroid regimen (per PEXIVAS protocol); prompt B-cell depletion with Rituximab; mandatory PJP prophylaxis with Bactrim; annual influenza, COVID-19, and pneumococcal vaccinations; avoidance of nephrotoxic drugs. Thresholds: Pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis on renal biopsy in the presence of positive MPO-ANCA without granulomatous inflammation.

patient_plain_language: An autoimmune small blood vessel inflammation that specifically attacks your kidney filters and the blood vessels in your lungs. It is driven by antibodies called MPO-ANCA (p-ANCA). Unlike its sibling disease GPA, it does not attack your nose or sinuses, but it can rapidly damage your kidneys if not treated. The landmark PEXIVAS trial proved that using a smarter, lower dose of steroid pills cures the disease just as well while saving patients from dangerous infections.

title: Rhabdomyolysis (Crush Injury & Myoglobinuric AKI): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (New England Journal of Medicine)
snippet: Skeletal muscle breakdown releases toxic intracellular contents (myoglobin, creatine kinase, potassium, phosphorus) into the circulation. Myoglobin induces acute kidney injury via renal vasoconstriction, direct proximal tubular cytotoxicity, and intratubular Tamm-Horsfall cast obstruction (acidic urine pH promotes cast formation). AGGRESSIVE ISOTONIC SALINE RESUSCITATION (infusing 500-1000 mL/h targeting urine output 200-300 mL/h) initiated within 6 hours of onset eliminates renal failure in >80% of patients. Guideline Protocol: EARLY AGGRESSIVE IV FLUID RESUSCITATION (normal saline 10-15 mL/kg/h targeting high urine flow); identify and treat compartment syndrome (emergent fasciotomy); discontinue inciting statins, fibrates, or recreational drugs; avoid aggressive calcium administration during early phase (causes metastatic tissue calcification). Thresholds: Serum CK >5-10 times the upper limit of normal (>1,000-5,000 U/L) with reddish-brown tea-colored urine positive for blood on dipstick but negative for RBCs on microscopy.
key_takeaway: Skeletal muscle breakdown releases toxic intracellular contents (myoglobin, creatine kinase, potassium, phosphorus) into the circulation. Myoglobin induces acute kidney injury via renal vasoconstriction, direct proximal ...
patient_plain_language: Severe muscle breakdown triggered by a crush injury, intense unaccustomed exercise, prolonged immobility on a hard floor, or certain medications (like statins). Damaged muscle fibers burst, pouring dark muscle pigment (myoglobin) into your bloodstream. The pigment clogs and poisons your kidney tubes, turning your urine dark reddish-brown like iced tea. Pumping large amounts of IV fluids immediately flushes the pigment safely out of your kidneys.

doctor_consultation_checklist.safety_question: Is my urine output being monitored with a catheter to ensure at least 200 to 300 mL of fluid flushes out every hour?
doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: Are my blood potassium levels being checked every few hours to prevent dangerous heart rhythm problems?

Sudden spike in blood potassium (>6.0 mEq/L) causing palpitations and peaked T-waves on ECG

solution_protocol.non_pharmacological_targets: EARLY AGGRESSIVE IV FLUID RESUSCITATION (normal saline 10-15 mL/kg/h targeting high urine flow); identify and treat compartment syndrome (emergent fasciotomy); discontinue inciting statins, fibrates, or recreational drugs; avoid aggressive calcium administration during early phase (causes metastatic tissue calcification).
solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK; peaks at 24-72h; CK >5,000 U/L indicates high AKI risk); serum potassium, phosphorus, calcium, and creatinine every 4-6 hours; urine output via Foley catheter.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Serum CK >5-10 times the upper limit of normal (>1,000-5,000 U/L) with reddish-brown tea-colored urine positive for blood on dipstick but negative for RBCs on microscopy.

stack_1_medlineplus.layman_summary: Rhabdomyolysis is rapid breakdown of muscle tissue releasing dark pigment that can clog and damage the kidneys.

stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Drink plenty of water after exercise, seek immediate emergency care for dark brown urine and muscle pain, and get IV fluids.

approved_drugs: Aggressive Isotonic Crystalloid IV Infusion (0.9% Normal Saline)
Sodium Bicarbonate IV (to alkalize urine pH >6.5 if non-hypocalcemic)

stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: Avoid giving IV Calcium for hypocalcemia unless life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias exist (causes metastatic tissue calcification).
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Loop diuretics (Furosemide) should ONLY be used AFTER adequate intravascular volume is restored.

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: Early aggressive crystalloid resuscitation within 6 hours reduces rhabdomyolysis acute kidney injury by over 80%.

title: Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury (CA-AKI / CIN): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (New England Journal of Medicine)
snippet: CA-AKI is an abrupt decline in renal function within 48-72 hours of intravascular iodinated contrast administration. The definitive landmark PRESERVE trial (n=5,177 high-risk patients undergoing angiography) proved that INTRAVENOUS ISOTONIC 0.9% SODIUM CHLORIDE was the gold standard, and that Sodium Bicarbonate or Oral N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) provided NO BENEFIT in preventing death, dialysis, or persistent renal decline. Use of low-osmolar or iso-osmolar contrast and minimizing contrast volume (Contrast Volume / eGFR ratio <3.0) prevents injury. Guideline Protocol: Pre- and post-procedure volume expansion with isotonic crystalloids (0.9% saline 1-1.5 mL/kg/h for 3-12 hours pre-procedure and 6-12 hours post-procedure); minimize iodinated contrast volume; hold non-essential nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) 48h prior; hold Metformin 48h post-contrast. Thresholds: Relative increase in serum creatinine >=25% or absolute increase >=0.3-0.5 mg/dL within 48-72 hours of contrast medium exposure.
key_takeaway: CA-AKI is an abrupt decline in renal function within 48-72 hours of intravascular iodinated contrast administration. The definitive landmark PRESERVE trial (n=5,177 high-risk patients undergoing angiography) proved that ...
patient_plain_language: A temporary decline in kidney function that can happen after receiving concentrated iodine contrast dye for a CT scan or heart catheterization. The dye temporarily narrows kidney blood vessels and causes oxygen stress. The landmark PRESERVE trial of over 5,000 patients showed that simple, regular IV saline fluid given before and after the scan protects your kidneys better than any special pills or fancy solutions.

solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Baseline serum creatinine and eGFR; follow-up serum creatinine at 48-72 hours post-contrast exposure.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Relative increase in serum creatinine >=25% or absolute increase >=0.3-0.5 mg/dL within 48-72 hours of contrast medium exposure.

stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: N-Acetylcysteine (Mucomyst) and Sodium Bicarbonate offer NO benefit over isotonic saline (proven by PRESERVE trial).
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Withhold Metformin at time of procedure and for 48 hours post-procedure until renal stability verified.

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: Isotonic saline is effective; N-acetylcysteine and sodium bicarbonate provide no benefit in preventing CA-AKI (p=0.75).

disease: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (Drug-Induced AIN - Triad Fever/Rash/Eosinophilia)
title: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (Drug-Induced AIN - Triad Fever/Rash/Eosinophilia): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Kidney International)
keywords: acute interstitial nephritis (drug-induced ain - triad fever/rash/eosinophilia)
snippet: Drug-induced AIN accounts for 15-20% of unexplained acute kidney injury, triggered by Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs), NSAIDs, Beta-lactam antibiotics, Ciprofloxacin, or Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICIs). The classic triad (fever, maculopapular rash, peripheral eosinophilia) is present in <10% of cases; sterile pyuria and white blood cell casts are common. EARLY DISCONTINUATION OF INCITING DRUG COMBINED WITH EARLY ORAL CORTICOSTEROIDS (Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day within 7-14 days) prevents irreversible interstitial fibrosis. Guideline Protocol: IMMEDIATELY DISCONTINUE ALL SUSPECTED INCITING DRUGS (PPIs, NSAIDs, antibiotics); avoid future re-challenge with the offending drug class; early initiation of oral corticosteroids if no improvement within 3-5 days of drug cessation. Thresholds: Unexplained acute rise in serum creatinine temporally related to a newly initiated medication, with interstitial inflammation on renal biopsy.
key_takeaway: Drug-induced AIN accounts for 15-20% of unexplained acute kidney injury, triggered by Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs), NSAIDs, Beta-lactam antibiotics, Ciprofloxacin, or Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICIs). The classic tri...
patient_plain_language: An allergic reaction deep inside the sponge tissue surrounding your kidney tubes (interstitium) caused by a medication—most commonly everyday heartburn pills (Prilosec/Nexium), pain relievers (ibuprofen/Advil), or antibiotics. White blood cells swarm into your kidneys, causing inflammation and kidney failure. Stopping the offending pill immediately and taking a short course of steroid pills heals the kidneys and prevents permanent scarring.

Low-grade fever and spreading itchy pink rash with joint pain and dark urine

solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Serial serum creatinine and BUN; urinalysis (checking for sterile pyuria, mild proteinuria <1g, and WBC casts); renal biopsy (gold standard demonstrating interstitial edema and lymphocytic/eosinophilic infiltrate).
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Unexplained acute rise in serum creatinine temporally related to a newly initiated medication, with interstitial inflammation on renal biopsy.

stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Monitor blood glucose and blood pressure during steroid course.

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: Early corticosteroid therapy within 14 days of drug cessation achieves complete renal recovery in >80% of AIN.

title: Myasthenia Gravis (AChR-Ab Post-Synaptic Junction Failure): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Lancet Neurology)
snippet: Myasthenia Gravis involves pathogenic autoantibodies (anti-AChR in 85%, anti-MuSK, anti-LRP4) blocking and destroying post-synaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, producing hallmark FATIGABLE muscle weakness (worsens with repetitive use, improves with rest). The phase 3 ADAPT trial (n=167) proved that neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) blocker EFGARTIGIMOD produced rapid, significant clinical improvement (68% responders vs 30% placebo; p<0.0001). Pyridostigmine provides symptomatic acetylcholinesterase inhibition; thymectomy is class I recommendation in non-thymomatous generalized AChR+ MG. Guideline Protocol: Thymectomy evaluation (MGTX trial proved thymectomy improves clinical scores and reduces prednisone requirements for 5 years in AChR+ patients age 18-65); avoid medications that worsen MG (aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, macrolides, beta-blockers, magnesium IV, iodinated contrast); energy conservation techniques. Thresholds: Serum Anti-AChR binding antibody positive, or repetitive nerve stimulation showing decremental compound muscle action potential (>10% decrement at 3 Hz).

patient_plain_language: An autoimmune condition where your immune system attacks the docking docks (acetylcholine receptors) on your muscle cells. Nerves can send signals, but the muscles cannot catch them. This causes hallmark 'fatigue weakness': your eyelids droop (ptosis), your vision goes double, and chewing or walking gets progressively weaker as the day goes on, but temporarily improves after a rest nap.

title: Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS - Pre-Synaptic P/Q-Type VGCC): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews & Lancet Neurology)
journal: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews & Lancet Neurology
keywords: cochrane database of systematic reviews & lancet neurology
lambert-eaton myasthenic syndrome (lems - pre-synaptic p/q-type vgcc)
snippet: Unlike Myasthenia Gravis, LEMS involves autoantibodies directed against PRE-SYNAPTIC P/Q-type Voltage-Gated Calcium Channels (VGCC), blocking calcium influx and preventing acetylcholine vesicle release. OVER 50-60% OF PATIENTS HAVE SMALL CELL LUNG CANCER (SCLC - Paraneoplastic LEMS). Clinical hallmark: PROXIMAL MUSCLE STRENGTH AND DEEP TENDON REFLEXES TEMPORARILY IMPROVE FOLLOWING BRIEF MAXIMUM EXERCISE (POST-EXERCISE FACILITATION). AMIFAMPRIDINE (3,4-diaminopyridine / 3,4-DAP) blocks potassium channels, prolonging nerve depolarization and restoring muscle strength (p<0.001). Guideline Protocol: MANDATORY ONCOLOGICAL SCREENING FOR UNDERLYING SMALL CELL LUNG CANCER (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis and 18F-FDG PET/CT; repeat screening every 3-6 months for at least 2 years if initially negative); physical therapy; fall prevention. Thresholds: Positive P/Q-type VGCC antibodies, proximal limb weakness, autonomic dysfunction (dry mouth, erectile dysfunction, sluggish pupils), and hyporeflexia with post-exercise reflex return.

patient_plain_language: A rare condition where antibodies block the microscopic calcium gates at the very tips of your nerves, preventing them from releasing the chemical that tells muscles to contract. Over half of patients have a hidden small cell lung tumor producing these antibodies. Unlike myasthenia gravis, your muscle strength actually feels STRONGER for a few seconds right after a short burst of exercise (post-exercise facilitation). A targeted pill (Amifampridine) restores nerve firing.

doctor_consultation_checklist.safety_question: Did nerve testing show post-exercise facilitation (muscle signals doubling after 10 seconds of exercise)?
doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: Am I taking Amifampridine (3,4-DAP) to keep the nerve channels open and restore my leg strength?

Autonomic failure causing severe orthostatic blackouts and urinary retention

solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Repetitive nerve stimulation (low frequency 3 Hz shows decremental response; high frequency 20-50 Hz or 10-second voluntary exercise shows pathognomonic INCREMENTAL RESPONSE >100%); VGCC antibody titers; autonomic testing.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Positive P/Q-type VGCC antibodies, proximal limb weakness, autonomic dysfunction (dry mouth, erectile dysfunction, sluggish pupils), and hyporeflexia with post-exercise reflex return.

title: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS - Mixed Upper & Lower Motor Neuron): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Neurology & Lancet Neurology)
keywords: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (als - mixed upper & lower motor neuron)
snippet: ALS is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder causing relentless loss of both Upper Motor Neurons (hyperreflexia, spasticity, positive Babinski sign) and Lower Motor Neurons (fasciculations, muscle atrophy, flaccid weakness). RILUZOLE (50 mg BID oral glutamatergic inhibitor) extends tracheostomy-free survival by 2-3 months. IV/oral EDARAVONE (Radicava; free radical scavenger) slows functional decline by 33% on the ALSFRS-R scale in early definite ALS (p=0.001). EARLY NON-INVASIVE VENTILATION (NIV/BiPAP for FVC <50-80%) extends survival by 7-12 months and preserves quality of life. Guideline Protocol: Early multidisciplinary ALS clinic enrollment (significantly prolongs survival); timely non-invasive ventilation (NIV/BiPAP for FVC <50-80% or orthopnea); early percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) feeding tube placement before FVC <50% to maintain nutrition; speech-generating assistive devices. Thresholds: El Escorial and Gold Coast Diagnostic Criteria: Simultaneous upper and lower motor neuron signs across >=2 body regions (bulbar, cervical, thoracic, lumbosacral) with documented progression.
key_takeaway: ALS is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder causing relentless loss of both Upper Motor Neurons (hyperreflexia, spasticity, positive Babinski sign) and Lower Motor Neurons (fasciculations, muscle atrophy, flaccid weakness)...
patient_plain_language: A motor neuron disease (often known as Lou Gehrig's disease) where the nerve cells that control your voluntary muscles gradually waste away. Because both upper nerves in the brain and lower nerves in the spinal cord are affected, it causes a combination of muscle twitching (fasciculations), shrinking (atrophy), and muscle stiffness. Multidisciplinary ALS clinic care, early nighttime breathing support (BiPAP), and protective medicines (Riluzole and Radicava) prolong survival and comfort.

doctor_consultation_checklist.parameter_question: What is my current Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) sitting and lying down, and is it time to begin non-invasive nighttime BiPAP?
doctor_consultation_checklist.safety_question: Am I taking Riluzole twice daily, and are my liver function enzymes being monitored every month?
doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: Have we discussed early placement of a PEG feeding tube while my lung breathing function is still strong enough for the procedure?

red_flags: Severe orthopnea (inability to breathe while lying flat on the back, indicating bilateral diaphragm paralysis)
Choking on thin liquids and rapid weight loss from progressive bulbar swallowing failure

solution_protocol.non_pharmacological_targets: Early multidisciplinary ALS clinic enrollment (significantly prolongs survival); timely non-invasive ventilation (NIV/BiPAP for FVC <50-80% or orthopnea); early percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) feeding tube placement before FVC <50% to maintain nutrition; speech-generating assistive devices.
solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R) monthly; upright and supine spirometry (FVC and MIP/MEP every 3 months; >20% supine FVC drop indicates diaphragmatic weakness); liver enzymes on riluzole.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: El Escorial and Gold Coast Diagnostic Criteria: Simultaneous upper and lower motor neuron signs across >=2 body regions (bulbar, cervical, thoracic, lumbosacral) with documented progression.

stack_1_medlineplus.layman_summary: ALS is a motor nerve disease causing gradual weakness of voluntary muscles throughout the body.
stack_1_medlineplus.plain_analogy: Telephone transmission poles and household wiring slowly breaking down, cutting off power to household appliances.
stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Attend an ALS specialty clinic, start nighttime breathing support (BiPAP) early, and use assistive technology.

approved_drugs: Riluzole oral (Rilutek 50 mg BID - Extends Survival)
stack_2_openfda.dosing_gdmt: Riluzole 50 mg orally every 12 hours on an empty stomach; Edaravone 60 mg IV daily x 14 days in first 28-day cycle, then 10 of 14 days.
stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: Riluzole causes asymptomatic liver transaminase elevations; check LFTs monthly x 3 months, then quarterly.
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Edaravone contains sodium bisulfite; contraindicated in severe sulfite allergy.

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: Edaravone slows ALS functional rating scale decline by 33% compared to placebo over 24 weeks (p=0.001).

title: Guillain-Barré Syndrome (Acute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews & Lancet Neurology)
journal: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews & Lancet Neurology
keywords: cochrane database of systematic reviews & lancet neurology
snippet: GBS is an acute autoimmune post-infectious demyelinating polyneuropathy (commonly following Campylobacter jejuni, CMV, or respiratory illness) presenting with RAPIDLY ASCENDING SYMMETRICAL FLACCID PARALYSIS, AREFLEXIA, and autonomic instability. CORTICOSTEROIDS ARE COMPLETELY INEFFECTIVE AND HARMFUL. INTRAVENOUS IMMUNOGLOBULIN (IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day x 5 days) OR THERAPEUTIC PLASMA EXCHANGE (PE 4-5 sessions) initiated within 2 weeks halts progression and significantly accelerates motor recovery. Guideline Protocol: Admit to ICU/stepdown for close respiratory mechanics monitoring (the '20/30/40 rule': FVC <20 mL/kg, MIP <-30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O indicates elective intubation); deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis; aggressive neuropathic pain management (gabapentin); physical therapy. Thresholds: CSF examination demonstrating ALBUMINOCYTOLOGIC DISSOCIATION (elevated protein >45-100 mg/dL with normal WBC count <5-10 cells/mcL); nerve conduction showing demyelinating features.
key_takeaway: GBS is an acute autoimmune post-infectious demyelinating polyneuropathy (commonly following Campylobacter jejuni, CMV, or respiratory illness) presenting with RAPIDLY ASCENDING SYMMETRICAL FLACCID PARALYSIS, AREFLEXIA, a...
patient_plain_language: A rapid, temporary immune reaction (often triggered by a stomach bug or cold 1 to 3 weeks earlier) where your immune system attacks the insulation (myelin) covering your peripheral nerves. Weakness starts in your toes and legs and climbs upward toward your chest, along with numbness and loss of reflexes. Corticosteroids do NOT work; emergency hospital care with IV antibody infusions (IVIG) or plasma filtering clears the attack while nerves heal.

doctor_consultation_checklist.parameter_question: Are my breathing parameters (Forced Vital Capacity and NIF) being measured every 2 to 4 hours to protect my lungs?
doctor_consultation_checklist.safety_question: Did my spinal tap show 'albuminocytologic dissociation' (high protein with zero infection cells)?
doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: Why are steroid medications strictly avoided, and have we started IVIG antibody infusions right away?

red_flags: Rapidly ascending paralysis reaching the chest with inability to count to 20 in a single breath (Emergency Intubation)
Severe blood pressure swings (from 200/110 to 70/40 mmHg) and heart rate drops (Dysautonomia Emergency)

solution_protocol.non_pharmacological_targets: Admit to ICU/stepdown for close respiratory mechanics monitoring (the '20/30/40 rule': FVC <20 mL/kg, MIP <-30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O indicates elective intubation); deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis; aggressive neuropathic pain management (gabapentin); physical therapy.
solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Serial bedside Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) and Negative Inspiratory Force (NIF) every 2-4 hours; continuous cardiac telemetry (fatal dysautonomia occurs in 20%); Erasmus GBS Outcome Score (EGOS).
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: CSF examination demonstrating ALBUMINOCYTOLOGIC DISSOCIATION (elevated protein >45-100 mg/dL with normal WBC count <5-10 cells/mcL); nerve conduction showing demyelinating features.

stack_1_medlineplus.layman_summary: Guillain-Barré syndrome is rapid autoimmune nerve inflammation causing ascending leg and body paralysis.
stack_1_medlineplus.plain_analogy: A lightning storm stripping the protective rubber coating off electrical power lines, cutting power to distant switches.
stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Seek emergency hospital ICU care immediately; early IVIG infusions stop nerve damage, and breathing must be monitored.

approved_drugs: Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day x 5 days - Class I)
Therapeutic Plasma Exchange (5 sessions over 10-14 days)
stack_2_openfda.dosing_gdmt: IVIG 2 g/kg total dose divided over 5 consecutive days (0.4 g/kg/day); or Plasma Exchange 200-250 mL/kg over 5 sessions.
stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: STRICT CONTRAINDICATION: Systemic Corticosteroids (Prednisone) DELAY recovery in GBS and are proven ineffective.
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: IVIG requires screening for IgA deficiency (anaphylaxis risk) and monitoring of renal function and aseptic meningitis.

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: IVIG and plasma exchange produce equivalent superior recovery, halving time on mechanical ventilation compared to supportive care.

title: Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy (CIDP): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Lancet Neurology)
snippet: CIDP is a chronic, progressive or relapsing-remitting symmetric sensorimotor polyradiculoneuropathy progressing for >8 WEEKS (differentiating it from acute GBS). Unlike GBS, CIDP RESPONDS WELL TO CORTICOSTEROIDS. The phase 3 PATH trial (n=245) proved that weekly SUB-CUTANEOUS IMMUNOGLOBULIN (SCIG 0.2 g/kg or 0.4 g/kg) achieved 67-78% relapse-free survival compared to 37% placebo (p=0.0007), providing convenient at-home maintenance. Guideline Protocol: Adherence to maintenance immunoglobulin or steroid-sparing therapy; supervised physical and occupational therapy; orthotic devices (ankle-foot orthoses / AFOs for bilateral foot drop); fall prevention. Thresholds: Electrodiagnostic evidence of primary demyelinating neuropathy (conduction velocity slowing, conduction block, prolonged distal latencies) in >=2 nerves, progressing for >=8 weeks.
key_takeaway: CIDP is a chronic, progressive or relapsing-remitting symmetric sensorimotor polyradiculoneuropathy progressing for >8 WEEKS (differentiating it from acute GBS). Unlike GBS, CIDP RESPONDS WELL TO CORTICOSTEROIDS. The pha...
patient_plain_language: A chronic, ongoing autoimmune condition where your immune system continuously damages the insulation around your nerves over months or years. Unlike GBS which strikes suddenly and heals, CIDP slowly causes weakness and numbness in both legs and arms that lasts longer than 2 months. Fortunately, CIDP responds very well to regular antibody infusions (IVIG or easy at-home under-the-skin SCIG) or steroid pills.

doctor_consultation_checklist.parameter_question: Did nerve conduction tests prove chronic demyelination across multiple nerves lasting longer than 8 weeks?
doctor_consultation_checklist.safety_question: Am I a candidate for at-home subcutaneous immunoglobulin (SCIG) self-injections instead of hospital IV infusions?
doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: What is my current INCAT disability score, and are my ankle-foot braces helping me walk safely?

red_flags: Rapid loss of hand grip strength making it impossible to hold utensils or turn doorknobs
Severe progressive sensory ataxia causing frequent falls in the dark

solution_protocol.non_pharmacological_targets: Adherence to maintenance immunoglobulin or steroid-sparing therapy; supervised physical and occupational therapy; orthotic devices (ankle-foot orthoses / AFOs for bilateral foot drop); fall prevention.
solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Inflammatory Neuropathy Cause and Treatment (INCAT) disability score and Medical Research Council (MRC) sum score every 3-6 months; annual electrodiagnostic testing.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Electrodiagnostic evidence of primary demyelinating neuropathy (conduction velocity slowing, conduction block, prolonged distal latencies) in >=2 nerves, progressing for >=8 weeks.

stack_1_medlineplus.layman_summary: CIDP is chronic, long-term autoimmune nerve inflammation causing progressive arm and leg weakness.
stack_1_medlineplus.plain_analogy: A slow, continuous chemical drip that constantly dissolves the rubber insulation off home electrical wiring.
stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Take your maintenance immunoglobulin infusions faithfully, use ankle braces to prevent tripping, and do physical therapy.

stack_2_openfda.dosing_gdmt: IVIG 2 g/kg divided over 2-5 days loading; followed by SCIG 0.2-0.4 g/kg once weekly at home.
stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: Monitor for systemic steroid complications if corticosteroids are chosen as first line (osteoporosis, hyperglycemia).
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: SCIG requires monitoring for local infusion-site swelling and erythema.

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: Subcutaneous immunoglobulin maintenance therapy prevents CIDP relapse in >78% of patients (p=0.0007).

title: Trigeminal Neuralgia (Tic Douloureux - Neurovascular Compression): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Neurology)
snippet: Classic TN involves paroxysmal, excruciating, electric shock-like lancinating unilateral facial pain in V2/V3 distributions, triggered by innocuous tactile stimuli (touching face, brushing teeth, chewing, breeze). Caused by neurovascular compression of the trigeminal root entry zone (most commonly superior cerebellar artery). CARBAMAZEPINE (200-1200 mg/day) or OXCARBAZEPINE is first-line medical therapy, achieving initial pain relief in >80%. MICROVASCULAR DECOMPRESSION (MVD / Jannetta procedure) provides definitive cure (>70-80% pain-free at 10 years). Guideline Protocol: Screening for HLA-B*1502 allele prior to carbamazepine in patients of Asian descent (prevents fatal SJS/TEN); avoid known tactile facial triggers; soft room-temperature diet during flares; neurosurgical consultation for MVD if refractory or drug-intolerant. Thresholds: Brief, unilateral, electric-shock-like pains, abrupt in onset and termination, strictly limited to the distribution of one or more divisions of the trigeminal nerve.
key_takeaway: Classic TN involves paroxysmal, excruciating, electric shock-like lancinating unilateral facial pain in V2/V3 distributions, triggered by innocuous tactile stimuli (touching face, brushing teeth, chewing, breeze). Caused...
patient_plain_language: Known as one of the most agonizing pains in human medicine ('Tic Douloureux'). An artery at the base of your brain pulses against your trigeminal facial nerve like a hammer on an exposed electrical wire. The slightest light touch—a cool breeze, brushing your teeth, or chewing—triggers lightning bolts of excruciating electrical pain shooting across your cheek or jaw. A specific nerve pill (Carbamazepine) or a keyhole brain surgery to pad the nerve (MVD) stops the pain completely.

doctor_consultation_checklist.parameter_question: Did a high-resolution 3D MRI (FIESTA sequence) reveal an artery compressing my trigeminal nerve root?
doctor_consultation_checklist.safety_question: Was my genetic test (HLA-B*1502) checked before starting Carbamazepine to prevent severe skin allergic reactions?
doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: Am I a candidate for Microvascular Decompression (MVD) surgery to place a tiny Teflon pad between the artery and nerve?

red_flags: Severe pain preventing eating and drinking, causing acute dehydration and rapid weight loss
Sudden spreading skin rash with fever or severe mouth ulcers on Carbamazepine (SJS/TEN Emergency)

solution_protocol.non_pharmacological_targets: Screening for HLA-B*1502 allele prior to carbamazepine in patients of Asian descent (prevents fatal SJS/TEN); avoid known tactile facial triggers; soft room-temperature diet during flares; neurosurgical consultation for MVD if refractory or drug-intolerant.
solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: High-resolution 3D T2-weighted MRI brain (CISS / FIESTA sequence) demonstrating neurovascular contact with the trigeminal nerve root; complete blood count, sodium, and liver function on carbamazepine.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Brief, unilateral, electric-shock-like pains, abrupt in onset and termination, strictly limited to the distribution of one or more divisions of the trigeminal nerve.

stack_1_medlineplus.layman_summary: Trigeminal neuralgia is excruciating, electric-shock facial pain triggered by light touches on the cheek or jaw.
stack_1_medlineplus.plain_analogy: An exposed high-voltage spark plug wire vibrating against a metal pipe, firing wild electrical shocks with every pulse.
stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Take your nerve pain medication faithfully, eat soft foods during pain flares, and consult neurosurgery for nerve padding.

approved_drugs: Carbamazepine oral (Tegretol - Class I First Line)
stack_2_openfda.dosing_gdmt: Carbamazepine 100-200 mg BID, titrated by 100-200 mg every 2-3 days to 400-1,200 mg/day in divided doses.
stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: BLACK BOX WARNING: Fatal dermatological reactions (SJS/TEN) and aplastic anemia/agranulocytosis; screen HLA-B*1502.
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Carbamazepine frequently induces hyponatremia (SIADH) and CYP3A4 auto-induction; check serum sodium and CBC.

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: Carbamazepine achieves complete initial pain relief in >80% of TN; MVD provides durable 10-year cure in >75%.

title: Sjögren's Disease (Anti-SSA/Ro Autoimmune Exocrinopathy): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases)
snippet: Sjögren's is a systemic autoimmune exocrinopathy characterized by lymphocytic infiltration of salivary and lacrimal glands, producing Keratoconjunctivitis Sicca (severe dry eyes) and Xerostomia (severe dry mouth). Autoantibodies (Anti-SSA/Ro in 70-80%, Anti-SSB/La) are diagnostic. SJÖGREN'S CARRIES A 15-TO-40-FOLD ELEVATED RISK OF NON-HODGKIN B-CELL LYMPHOMA (MALT lymphoma of the parotid). Muscarinic agonists (Pilocarpine, Cevimeline) stimulate secretion; Hydroxychloroquine treats systemic arthralgias. Guideline Protocol: Preservative-free artificial tears and lubricating ophthalmic ointments; frequent sips of water, sugar-free gum/lozenges containing xylitol; intensive preventive dental hygiene every 3-4 months (loss of saliva accelerates rampant dental caries); avoid anticholinergic medications. Thresholds: ACR-EULAR score >=4 points (Anti-SSA positive = 3 points; labial salivary gland biopsy with focus score >=1 focus/4 mm2 = 3 points).
key_takeaway: Sjögren's is a systemic autoimmune exocrinopathy characterized by lymphocytic infiltration of salivary and lacrimal glands, producing Keratoconjunctivitis Sicca (severe dry eyes) and Xerostomia (severe dry mouth). Autoan...
patient_plain_language: An autoimmune condition where your immune cells attack and dry out the moisture-producing glands in your body, particularly your tear glands and salivary glands. Your eyes feel like they are full of sandpaper or grit, and your mouth becomes so dry you cannot swallow dry crackers without water. Because saliva protects your teeth, aggressive dental care is critical, and doctors must monitor for swollen parotid glands to screen for lymphoma.

doctor_consultation_checklist.parameter_question: Did my blood tests show positive Anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies or did a lip biopsy show lymphocytic focus score >=1?
doctor_consultation_checklist.safety_question: Have I been prescribed Pilocarpine or Cevimeline pills to stimulate natural saliva and tear production?
doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: Am I using preservative-free lubricating eye drops and seeing my dentist every 3 to 4 months for fluoride treatments?

red_flags: Rapid, firm, persistent enlargement of one parotid salivary gland in the cheek (B-Cell MALT Lymphoma)
Persistent dry eyes developing corneal ulceration or severe visual blurring

solution_protocol.non_pharmacological_targets: Preservative-free artificial tears and lubricating ophthalmic ointments; frequent sips of water, sugar-free gum/lozenges containing xylitol; intensive preventive dental hygiene every 3-4 months (loss of saliva accelerates rampant dental caries); avoid anticholinergic medications.
solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Ocular Staining Score (OSS) with lissamine green / fluorescein; Schirmer test (<=5 mm wetting at 5 min is abnormal); unstimulated whole salivary flow rate (<=0.1 mL/min); annual palpation of parotid glands and serum protein electrophoresis for M-spike (lymphoma surveillance).
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: ACR-EULAR score >=4 points (Anti-SSA positive = 3 points; labial salivary gland biopsy with focus score >=1 focus/4 mm2 = 3 points).

stack_1_medlineplus.layman_summary: Sjögren's disease is an autoimmune condition causing severe dry eyes and dry mouth by attacking moisture glands.
stack_1_medlineplus.plain_analogy: An automated lawn sprinkler line whose water supply valves have rusted shut, drying out the grass and plants.
stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Use preservative-free eye drops hourly, chew xylitol gum, brush and floss diligently, and report cheek swellings.

stack_2_openfda.dosing_gdmt: Pilocarpine 5 mg orally 3-4 times daily with meals; Cevimeline 30 mg TID; Hydroxychloroquine 5 mg/kg/day.
stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: Pilocarpine can cause profuse diaphoresis, urinary urgency, and bronchospasm (avoid in severe asthma).
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Lifelong ophthalmology screening for hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity.

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: Muscarinic agonists combined with topical cyclosporine significantly improve tear film stability and salivary flow.

disease: Diffuse Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (Anti-Scl-70 / Scleroderma Renal Crisis)
title: Diffuse Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (Anti-Scl-70 / Scleroderma Renal Crisis): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases)
keywords: diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (anti-scl-70 / scleroderma renal crisis)
snippet: Diffuse systemic sclerosis causes widespread skin fibrosis proximal to elbows/knees, driven by vasculopathy and autoantibodies (Anti-Scl-70 / Topoisomerase I in 30%, Anti-RNA Polymerase III). Anti-RNA Polymerase III carries high risk for SCLERODERMA RENAL CRISIS (SRC: acute malignant hypertension, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, and oliguric AKI). ACE INHIBITORS (CAPTOPRIL TITRATED AGGRESSIVELY) ARE LIFE-SAVING FOR SRC. CORTICOSTEROIDS (PREDNISONE >15 MG/DAY) DIRECTLY PRECIPITATE RENAL CRISIS AND ARE STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED. Guideline Protocol: MANDATORY HOME BLOOD PRESSURE MONITORING DAILY (any systolic BP rise >20-30 mmHg requires immediate emergency contact); cold protection for severe Raynaud's; early esophageal reflux management with high-dose PPI; lung screening. Thresholds: Skin thickening proximal to elbows and knees, Raynaud phenomenon with abnormal nailfold capillaroscopy, and positive Anti-Scl-70 or Anti-RNA Polymerase III antibodies.
key_takeaway: Diffuse systemic sclerosis causes widespread skin fibrosis proximal to elbows/knees, driven by vasculopathy and autoantibodies (Anti-Scl-70 / Topoisomerase I in 30%, Anti-RNA Polymerase III). Anti-RNA Polymerase III carr...
patient_plain_language: A serious autoimmune condition where your body overproduces collagen scar tissue throughout your skin and internal organs. The skin on your fingers, arms, chest, and face becomes tight, shiny, and hard like leather. It can cause blood vessel spasms (Raynaud's), heartburn, lung scarring, and sudden kidney crises. Steroids are dangerous poisons in this condition because they trigger kidney failure, but blood pressure pills (Captopril) protect your kidneys.

doctor_consultation_checklist.parameter_question: Do I carry the Anti-RNA Polymerase III antibody that puts me at high risk for Scleroderma Renal Crisis?
doctor_consultation_checklist.safety_question: Why is taking high-dose Prednisone steroid pills strictly forbidden for my diffuse scleroderma?
doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: Why is taking my blood pressure at home every single morning the most important life-saving habit I can have?

red_flags: Sudden jump in blood pressure (>140/90 mmHg or 20 mmHg increase) with headache and blurry vision (Scleroderma Renal Crisis - EMERGENCY CAPTOPRIL)
Rapidly worsening shortness of breath indicating aggressive Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD)

solution_protocol.non_pharmacological_targets: MANDATORY HOME BLOOD PRESSURE MONITORING DAILY (any systolic BP rise >20-30 mmHg requires immediate emergency contact); cold protection for severe Raynaud's; early esophageal reflux management with high-dose PPI; lung screening.
solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Annual High-Resolution Chest CT (HRCT) and PFTs (FVC and DLCO) for Interstitial Lung Disease; annual echocardiogram and NT-proBNP for Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension; daily home BP log.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Skin thickening proximal to elbows and knees, Raynaud phenomenon with abnormal nailfold capillaroscopy, and positive Anti-Scl-70 or Anti-RNA Polymerase III antibodies.

stack_1_medlineplus.layman_summary: Diffuse scleroderma is an autoimmune disease causing tightening of the skin and scarring of kidneys and lungs.
stack_1_medlineplus.plain_analogy: A flexible leather jacket left outside in a deep freeze that turns stiff, hard, and unbendable.
stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Check and record your blood pressure every single morning at home, keep your hands warm, and never take high-dose steroids.

approved_drugs: Captopril oral (Short-Acting ACEi - LIFE-SAVING FOR RENAL CRISIS)
Mycophenolate Mofetil (CellCept for progressive skin/lung disease)
stack_2_openfda.dosing_gdmt: Captopril 12.5-25 mg q8h rapidly titrated to max 100 mg TID targeting SBP 110-120 mmHg; Mycophenolate 1-1.5 g BID.
stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: STRICT CONTRAINDICATION: Corticosteroids (Prednisone >15 mg/day) directly trigger fatal Scleroderma Renal Crisis.
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Avoid beta-blockers (exacerbate severe peripheral Raynaud vasospasm and digital ulceration).

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: Early prompt ACE inhibitor therapy reduces 1-year mortality in Scleroderma Renal Crisis from >85% to <25%.

disease: Limited Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (CREST Syndrome / Anti-Centromere)
title: Limited Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (CREST Syndrome / Anti-Centromere): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases)
keywords: limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (crest syndrome / anti-centromere)
snippet: Limited cutaneous SSc is defined by skin thickening restricted to hands, face, and distal extremities, characterized by the classic CREST SYNDROME: Calcinosis cutis, Raynaud phenomenon, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, and Telangiectasia. Strongly associated with ANTI-CENTROMERE ANTIBODIES (ACA in >70-80%). Unlike diffuse SSc, limited SSc has low risk of renal crisis or severe ILD, but carries a high 10-15% cumulative risk of LATE-ONSET PULMONARY ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION (PAH). ANNUAL SCREENING WITH ECHOCARDIOGRAM, DLCO, AND THE DETECT ALGORITHM IS MANDATORY. Guideline Protocol: MANDATORY ANNUAL SCREENING FOR PULMONARY ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION (DETECT algorithm, DLCO, and echo); strict cold avoidance and heated gloves for Raynaud's; prompt treatment of infected digital ulcers; elevate head of bed for reflux. Thresholds: Anti-Centromere Antibodies (ACA positive) with distal sclerodactyly, Raynaud's, and telangiectasias on face/hands.
key_takeaway: Limited cutaneous SSc is defined by skin thickening restricted to hands, face, and distal extremities, characterized by the classic CREST SYNDROME: Calcinosis cutis, Raynaud phenomenon, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodact...
patient_plain_language: A milder, slower-moving form of scleroderma often called CREST syndrome. Skin thickening is limited to your fingers and face. The 5 hallmark signs are: calcium lumps under the skin, cold white fingers in the cold (Raynaud's), heartburn difficulty swallowing, claw-like finger tightening (sclerodactyly), and red spider spots on your lips and palms (telangiectasias). The main long-term danger is developing high blood pressure in your lungs (PAH), so a yearly heart ultrasound is essential.

doctor_consultation_checklist.parameter_question: Did blood tests confirm Anti-Centromere Antibodies (ACA)?
doctor_consultation_checklist.safety_question: Is my annual echocardiogram and lung diffusion (DLCO) breathing test scheduled to detect early pulmonary hypertension?
doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: What medications (like calcium channel blockers or sildenafil) will protect my fingers from painful cold-induced sores?

red_flags: New-onset shortness of breath when walking flat ground, with lightheadedness (Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension)
Painful, black, infected ulcers on the tips of the fingers (Digital Gangrene from severe Raynaud's)

solution_protocol.non_pharmacological_targets: MANDATORY ANNUAL SCREENING FOR PULMONARY ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION (DETECT algorithm, DLCO, and echo); strict cold avoidance and heated gloves for Raynaud's; prompt treatment of infected digital ulcers; elevate head of bed for reflux.
solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Annual echocardiogram (measuring tricuspid regurgitant jet velocity); annual PFTs (disproportionate drop in DLCO with preserved FVC is the earliest red flag for PAH); annual NT-proBNP.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Anti-Centromere Antibodies (ACA positive) with distal sclerodactyly, Raynaud's, and telangiectasias on face/hands.

stack_1_medlineplus.layman_summary: Limited scleroderma (CREST) causes cold-sensitive white fingers, heartburn, tight skin on fingers, and lung pressure risk.
stack_1_medlineplus.plain_analogy: Rubber bands wound tightly around the fingers while cold wind causes the small fuel pipes to freeze shut.
stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Wear heated mittens in cold weather, take your reflux medicine, and get a yearly heart ultrasound to check lung pressure.

approved_drugs: Sildenafil oral (Viagra for refractory Raynaud's/digital ulcers)
stack_2_openfda.dosing_gdmt: Nifedipine ER 30-60 mg daily; Sildenafil 20 mg TID for ischemic digital ulcers; high-dose PPI therapy.
stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: Avoid beta-blockers and triptan migraine medications (trigger severe peripheral arterial vasospasm).
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Dose adjustments for hepatic and renal function with PDE5 inhibitors.

disease: Ankylosing Spondylitis (Axial Spondyloarthritis - HLA-B27 Bamboo Spine)

snippet: Axial spondyloarthritis is characterized by immune inflammation of the sacroiliac joints (sacroiliitis) and spine, driven by HLA-B27 and the IL-23/IL-17 pathway, causing syndesmophyte formation and spinal fusion ('Bamboo Spine'). Hallmark: INFLAMMATORY BACK PAIN (onset age <40, insidious onset, IMPROVES WITH EXERCISE, WORSENS WITH REST, nocturnal back pain). CONTINUOUS NSAIDs (Celecoxib, Naproxen) are first-line; Biologics (TNF INHIBITORS like Adalimumab/Infliximab or IL-17 INHIBITORS like Secukinumab/Ixekizumab) achieve ASAS40 response in >60% and arrest radiographic spinal progression. Guideline Protocol: Lifelong regular physical exercise and spinal extension physical therapy (preserves chest expansion and spinal mobility; swimming and daily stretching are foundational); complete smoking cessation (smoking accelerates spinal fusion and syndesmophyte growth); maintain erect posture. Thresholds: Radiographic sacroiliitis on pelvic X-ray (modified New York criteria) or active sacroiliac bone marrow edema on MRI (ASAS criteria) in a patient with chronic inflammatory back pain.

patient_plain_language: An autoimmune arthritis that attacks your lower back and pelvic joints (sacroiliac joints), strongly linked to the HLA-B27 gene. Unlike common mechanical back pain, this pain is worst in the morning with stiffness lasting over 30 minutes, feels BETTER when you walk or exercise, and wakes you up in the second half of the night. If untreated, bones in the spine fuse together like solid bamboo. Daily stretching, anti-inflammatory pills, and biologic injections keep your spine flexible.

Guideline Protocol: Gradual slow corticosteroid taper over 12-24 months (rapid tapering triggers relapse in >50%); osteoporosis prophylaxis (calcium, vitamin D, and bisphosphonate); regular low-impact exercise. Thresholds: Age >=50, bilateral shoulder and hip girdle aching with morning stiffness >45 minutes, elevated ESR/CRP, and dramatic >70% symptom relief within 72 hours of low-dose prednisone.

snippet: Dermatomyositis is an immune-mediated necrotizing microangiopathy of skin and skeletal muscle. Thresholds: Pathognomonic skin lesions (Gottron papules or heliotrope rash) with proximal muscle weakness, elevated CK, and muscle biopsy demonstrating perifascicular atrophy.

It causes a distinctive purplish rash over your eyelids (heliotrope rash) and red, scaly bumps across your knuckles (Gottron's papules), along with weakness in your shoulders and thighs. Because it is frequently triggered by a hidden cancer, thorough full-body cancer screening is mandatory.

title: Bullous Pemphigoid (BP180/BP230 Subepidermal Tense Blisters): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (British Journal of Dermatology & Cochrane Reviews)

snippet: Bullous pemphigoid is the most common autoimmune blistering disease, predominantly affecting elderly individuals (>70 years), frequently linked to neurological comorbidities (dementia, Parkinson's) or DPP-4 inhibitors (gliptins). Pathogenic autoantibodies target hemidesmosomal adhesion proteins BP180 and BP230 at the dermal-epidermal junction. Produces TENSE SUBEPIDERMAL BULLAE ON ERYTHEMATOUS BASES WITH NEGATIVE NIKOLSKY SIGN. HIGH-POTENCY TOPICAL CORTICOSTEROIDS (Clobetasol propionate cream 20-30 g/day) are EQUALLY EFFECTIVE TO ORAL STEROIDS WITH SIGNIFICANTLY LOWER 1-YEAR MORTALITY (Lancet landmark trial). Guideline Protocol: Discontinue potential drug culprits (DPP-4 inhibitors / gliptins, loop diuretics, PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors); gentle skin care (avoid friction and adhesive tape); sterile lancing of large tense blisters (leave blister roofs intact as biological dressings); daily clobetasol cream application. Thresholds: Subepidermal blister split on H&E biopsy, with linear deposition of IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone on direct immunofluorescence (DIF).

Because the split is deep, it causes thick, taut, dome-shaped blisters ('tense bullae') that do not pop easily, often starting with intense itching. Rubbing high-strength steroid cream (Clobetasol) all over the skin heals the blisters just as well as steroid pills with far fewer side effects.

snippet: Pemphigus vulgaris is a potentially fatal intraepidermal blistering disorder caused by IgG autoantibodies targeting desmoglein 3 (mucosal-predominant) and desmoglein 1 (mucocutaneous). snippet: MGUS is an asymptomatic premalignant plasma cell precursor condition present in >3-5% of adults over 50. Defined by: 1) Serum monoclonal protein (M-protein) <30 g/L (<3.0 g/dL); 2) Clonal bone marrow plasma cells <10%; 3) ABSOLUTE ABSENCE OF END-ORGAN DAMAGE (NO CRAB FEATURES: normal calcium, normal renal function, normal hemoglobin, and absence of lytic bone lesions on skeletal imaging). Progresses to multiple myeloma or related disorders at a constant rate of 1% per year. MANAGEMENT IS STRICT OBSERVATION (WATCH-AND-WAIT); CHEMOTHERAPY OR IMMUNOTHERAPY IS STRICTLY HARMFUL. Guideline Protocol: NO ACTIVE CHEMOTHERAPY OR IMMUNOSUPPRESSION; reassuring patient of low annual progression risk (1% per year); healthy lifestyle; prompt evaluation if bone pain, fatigue, or unexplained weight loss develops. Thresholds: Serum M-protein <3.0 g/dL with bone marrow plasma cells <10% and complete absence of CRAB symptoms or amyloidosis.

patient_plain_language: A common, silent blood finding where a small cluster of plasma cells produces a small amount of extra antibody protein (M-spike) in your blood. It is NOT active cancer and causes ZERO symptoms, zero bone damage, and zero kidney damage. Over 99% of people live completely normal lifespans with no issues. The risk of it ever turning into active myeloma is only about 1% per year, so no treatment or chemo is needed—just a simple yearly blood check.

solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Serum M-protein <3.0 g/dL with bone marrow plasma cells <10% and complete absence of CRAB symptoms or amyloidosis.

stack_1_medlineplus.layman_summary: MGUS is a benign precursor protein in the blood that requires routine monitoring but no treatment.
stack_1_medlineplus.plain_analogy: A small, harmless mole on your skin that is not cancer, but that you have checked by a doctor once a year.
stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Live your life normally, stay active, avoid unneeded cancer worry, and attend your yearly blood checkup.

approved_drugs: Active Surveillance / Watch-and-Wait (Class I Standard of Care)

stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: DO NOT treat MGUS with chemotherapy, proteasome inhibitors, or steroids (pure toxicity with zero survival benefit).
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Bone density monitoring with DXA scan (MGUS carries slightly increased risk of osteoporosis).

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: MGUS progresses to myeloma at a constant rate of 1% per year; 50-year follow-up confirms observation is standard.

disease: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL - Del(17p)/TP53 & BTK Inhibitors)
title: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL - Del(17p)/TP53 & BTK Inhibitors): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (New England Journal of Medicine)
keywords: chronic lymphocytic leukemia (cll - del(17p)/tp53 & btk inhibitors)
snippet: CLL is a clonal proliferation of mature CD5+/CD19+/CD23+ B-cells. Asymptomatic early stage (Rai 0 / Binet A) requires observation ('watch and wait'). For symptomatic or high-risk disease (del(17p) or TP53 mutation, which confers chemo-refractory biology), TARGETED CHEMO-FREE GDMT IS MANDATORY. The head-to-head phase 3 ALPINE trial (n=652) proved that second-generation BTK inhibitor ZANUBRUTINIB achieved superior Progression-Free Survival (hazard ratio 0.65; p=0.002) and significantly lower atrial fibrillation rates (5.2% vs 13.3%) compared to first-generation Ibrutinib. Fixed-duration Venetoclax + Obinutuzumab is alternative frontline. Guideline Protocol: Watchful waiting for asymptomatic Rai Stage 0 disease; non-live vaccinations (influenza, pneumococcal, recombinant zoster Shingrix); aggressive sun protection (CLL multiplies non-melanoma skin cancer risk 8-fold); prompt treatment of bacterial infections. Thresholds: Monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis >=5,000/mcL (>=5.0 x 10^9/L) in peripheral blood with characteristic CD5, CD19, CD20 (dim), and CD23 co-expression on flow cytometry.
key_takeaway: CLL is a clonal proliferation of mature CD5+/CD19+/CD23+ B-cells. Asymptomatic early stage (Rai 0 / Binet A) requires observation ('watch and wait'). For symptomatic or high-risk disease (del(17p) or TP53 mutation, which...
patient_plain_language: The most common leukemia in adults. Your bone marrow produces too many mature-looking white blood cells (lymphocytes). In its early stages, it causes no symptoms and patients live for decades without ever needing treatment ('watch and wait'). When treatment is eventually needed, modern medicine uses gentle, targeted chemo-free pills like Zanubrutinib that block a specific cancer enzyme (BTK) with far fewer side effects.

Severe fatigue and shortness of breath indicating rapid autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA)

stack_1_medlineplus.plain_analogy: A city park where old pigeons refuse to fly away and slowly crowd the pathways, but cause no immediate danger.
stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Stay up to date on non-live vaccines, protect your skin from sun damage, and attend regular blood count checks.

stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: BTK inhibitors increase bleeding risks (hold prior to major surgery) and risk of atrial fibrillation/hypertension.
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Venetoclax carries black box warning for fatal Tumor Lysis Syndrome; mandatory 5-week ramp-up with hydration/allopurinol.

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: Zanubrutinib achieves superior progression-free survival over ibrutinib with 60% lower atrial fibrillation risk (p=0.002).

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML - Auer Rods & Targeted 7+3 Induction)
title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML - Auer Rods & Targeted 7+3 Induction): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (New England Journal of Medicine)
keywords: acute myeloid leukemia (aml - auer rods & targeted 7+3 induction)
snippet: AML is an aggressive hematologic emergency characterized by clonal expansion of poorly differentiated myeloid precursors (blasts >=20% in bone marrow/blood) with presence of AUER RODS on microscopy. In fit younger patients, intensive '7+3' induction (Cytarabine 7 days + Daunorubicin 3 days) combined with targeted agents (Midostaurin for FLT3-mutated; Gemtuzumab ozogamicin for CD33+) is standard. In unfit or older patients (>=75 years), the landmark VIALE-A trial (n=431) revolutionized therapy: AZACITIDINE + BCL-2 INHIBITOR VENETOCLAX significantly prolonged overall survival (14.7 vs 9.6 months; hazard ratio 0.66; p<0.001) and doubled complete remission rates (66.4% vs 28.3%). Guideline Protocol: EMERGENT HOSPITAL ADMISSION; infection prophylaxis during prolonged neutropenia (Posaconazole antifungal, Levofloxacin, Acyclovir); allopurinol/rasburicase and brisk IV hydration to prevent Tumor Lysis Syndrome; blood product transfusion support (platelets >10,000/mcL). Thresholds: >=20% myeloblasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood, or presence of AML-defining cytogenetics [t(8;21), inv(16), t(15;17)] regardless of blast count.

patient_plain_language: An aggressive, fast-moving cancer of the blood where your bone marrow fills with immature, non-working white blood cells called myeloblasts. Because blasts crowd out normal cells, you rapidly become severely anemic, vulnerable to life-threatening infections, and bleed easily. For patients who cannot handle intense hospital chemotherapy, modern combination therapy using Azacitidine with a targeted pill called Venetoclax produces dramatic remissions.

doctor_consultation_checklist.safety_question: Am I a candidate for standard intensive 7+3 chemotherapy or the gentler targeted Azacitidine + Venetoclax regimen?
doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: Are preventive antifungal (Posaconazole) and antibiotic medicines protecting me while my white blood cells are low?

red_flags: Sudden high fever (>38.3 C) during low white blood cell count (Febrile Neutropenia - Emergency IV Antibiotics within 60 min)
Spontaneous bleeding from gums, nose, or urine indicating severe thrombocytopenia or DIC

solution_protocol.non_pharmacological_targets: EMERGENT HOSPITAL ADMISSION; infection prophylaxis during prolonged neutropenia (Posaconazole antifungal, Levofloxacin, Acyclovir); allopurinol/rasburicase and brisk IV hydration to prevent Tumor Lysis Syndrome; blood product transfusion support (platelets >10,000/mcL).
solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Bone marrow biopsy at Day 14 and Day 28 post-induction to evaluate blast clearance (<5% blasts defines morphologic remission); daily CBC, coagulation, and comprehensive metabolic panel; molecular NGS testing (FLT3, NPM1, CEBPA, IDH1, IDH2, TP53).
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: >=20% myeloblasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood, or presence of AML-defining cytogenetics [t(8;21), inv(16), t(15;17)] regardless of blast count.

stack_1_medlineplus.layman_summary: AML is a rapidly progressing leukemia where immature blast cells crowd the bone marrow, requiring urgent treatment.
stack_1_medlineplus.plain_analogy: Weeds rapidly overrunning a vegetable garden within days, choking out all the tomatoes and carrots.
stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Seek immediate emergency hospital oncology care for high fever or unexplained bleeding, and stay in protected isolation.

approved_drugs: Azacitidine SubQ/IV + Venetoclax oral (VIALE-A Frontline Standard)
stack_2_openfda.dosing_gdmt: Venetoclax 400 mg daily (with ramp-up) + Azacitidine 75 mg/m2 daily x 7 days every 28 days; or 7+3 induction.
stack_2_openfda.black_box_warning: Extreme neutropenia and fatal infectious complications occur during induction; posaconazole prophylaxis is mandatory.
stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Venetoclax dose must be reduced by 75% when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (posaconazole).

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: Azacitidine plus Venetoclax extends overall survival by 50% and achieves 66% remission in AML (p<0.001).

title: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma (Reed-Sternberg Cells & Nivolumab-AVD): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (New England Journal of Medicine)
snippet: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma (cHL) is characterized by giant multinucleated REED-STERNBERG CELLS (CD30+, CD15+) surrounded by an extensive reactive inflammatory background, frequently presenting in adolescents and young adults with painless rubbery cervical lymphadenopathy and B-symptoms (fever, drenching night sweats, weight loss). The definitive landmark SWOG S1826 phase 3 trial (n=970) proved that PD-1 INHIBITOR NIVOLUMAB COMBINED WITH AVD CHEMOTHERAPY achieved 94% 2-year progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.48; p<0.001) versus Brentuximab-AVD, with significantly lower neuropathy, establishing N-AVD as the new global frontline standard. Guideline Protocol: Prompt initiation of curative-intent chemoimmunotherapy; fertility preservation counseling and sperm/oocyte banking prior to treatment; interim PET/CT (Deauville criteria) to guide response-adapted therapy; cardiac and pulmonary function monitoring. Thresholds: Excisional lymph node biopsy demonstrating CD30+ CD15+ Reed-Sternberg cells on immunohistochemistry.

patient_plain_language: A highly curable cancer of the lymphatic system that most often affects teenagers and young adults. It begins as a painless, rubbery lump in your neck or collarbone, sometimes with drenching night sweats and fevers. Under a microscope, pathognomonic giant cancer cells look like owl eyes (Reed-Sternberg cells). Modern treatment combining immunotherapy (Nivolumab) with chemotherapy cures over 94% of patients while protecting nerves and fertility.

doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: Have we discussed fertility preservation (freezing eggs or sperm) before my first infusion?

Severe shortness of breath or cough indicating treatment-related pneumonitis

solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: 18F-FDG PET/CT at baseline, after cycle 2 (interim PET: Deauville score 1-3 indicates complete metabolic response), and at end-of-treatment; serial CBC and liver/thyroid panels on nivolumab.
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Excisional lymph node biopsy demonstrating CD30+ CD15+ Reed-Sternberg cells on immunohistochemistry.

stack_3_pubmed_cebm.endpoints: Nivolumab-AVD achieves 94% 2-year progression-free survival in advanced Hodgkin lymphoma (p<0.001).

disease: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL - Pola-R-CHP & CAR-T Therapy)
title: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL - Pola-R-CHP & CAR-T Therapy): Evidence & Clinical Guidelines (New England Journal of Medicine)
keywords: diffuse large b-cell lymphoma (dlbcl - pola-r-chp & car-t therapy)
snippet: DLBCL is the most common aggressive Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma, characterized by diffuse sheets of large atypical CD20+ B-cells with high proliferative index (Ki-67 >70-80%). The landmark phase 3 POLARIX trial (n=879) proved that replacing vincristine with antibody-drug conjugate Polatuzumab Vedotin (Pola-R-CHP: Polatuzumab + Rituximab + Cyclophosphamide + Doxorubicin + Prednisone) achieved a 27% reduction in risk of progression, relapse, or death compared to standard R-CHOP (p=0.02). In primary refractory or early relapsed DLBCL (<=12 months), CD19 CAR T-CELL THERAPY (Axicabtagene ciloleucel; ZUMA-7 trial) quadrupled 2-year event-free survival (40.5% vs 16.3%; p<0.001) over autologous stem cell transplant. Guideline Protocol: Prompt initiation of curative-intent chemoimmunotherapy; CNS prophylaxis (intrathecal methotrexate) for high CNS-IPI score; allopurinol/rasburicase for Tumor Lysis Syndrome; G-CSF (Pegfilgrastim) primary prophylaxis for febrile neutropenia. Thresholds: Diffuse effacement of lymph node architecture by large B-cells expressing CD20 with Ki-67 >60-90% on excisional biopsy.

patient_plain_language: The most common aggressive lymphoma in adults. Cancerous B-cells multiply rapidly in your lymph nodes, forming rapidly enlarging masses in your neck, armpits, abdomen, or groin. Although fast-growing, it is highly curable with intensive treatment. Modern frontline therapy uses an antibody-drug smart bomb (Polatuzumab) combined with chemo (Pola-R-CHP). If the lymphoma ever returns, miraculous living cell therapy (CAR-T cells), where your own immune cells are genetically re-engineered to hunt down and kill cancer cells, cures over 40% of relapsed patients.

doctor_consultation_checklist.safety_question: Am I receiving the modern Pola-R-CHP regimen (with Polatuzumab Vedotin) shown to improve cure rates over old R-CHOP?
doctor_consultation_checklist.action_threshold_question: If my lymphoma does not fully disappear, am I a candidate for personalized CAR-T cell immunotherapy?

Facial swelling, neck fullness, and dilated chest veins (Superior Vena Cava Syndrome Emergency)

solution_protocol.monitoring_cadence: Baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT and end-of-treatment PET/CT (Lugano 2014 criteria); International Prognostic Index (IPI score); cell of origin classification (Hans algorithm: GCB vs ABC/non-GCB); FISH for MYC, BCL2, BCL6 ('double-hit' lymphoma).
solution_protocol.clinical_thresholds: Diffuse effacement of lymph node architecture by large B-cells expressing CD20 with Ki-67 >60-90% on excisional biopsy.

stack_1_medlineplus.layman_summary: DLBCL is an aggressive but curable cancer of white blood cells, treated with smart-bomb antibody chemo or CAR-T cells.
stack_1_medlineplus.plain_analogy: A rapid wildfire blazing through dry brush that can be completely extinguished if doused immediately with heavy fire retardant.
stack_1_medlineplus.lifestyle_action: Attend all chemo cycles on schedule, protect yourself from infections, and attend end-of-treatment PET scans.

Axicabtagene Ciloleucel (Yescarta - CD19 CAR-T for Relapse)

stack_2_openfda.organ_clearance_cutoffs: Dose reduction of cyclophosphamide/doxorubicin in severe hepatic or renal dysfunction.
